## FIXED-808 — A stale Permissions tab could overwrite a newer decision

**Severity: Medium. Area: Permissions. Status: Fixed 2026-10-05. §13.2 item 6
for permission changes.**

**Observed.** A tab opened before a permission was tightened elsewhere still
offered the old value, and a change from it applied over the newer one with
no sign anything was overwritten — including undoing a tightening.

**Fixed.** Decision-mode and gate changes accept the value the page showed
(`expected_mode`, `expected_state`); a mismatch is `409 capability_conflict`
and nothing changes. Permissions sends what it displays on every single, bulk
and step-up change, and on a conflict closes any dialog, says *This permission
was changed somewhere else since this page loaded, so nothing was changed*, and
re-reads the page. Clients that send no expected value behave as before.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_api_decision_modes.py` (three cases);
`CapabilitiesView.test.ts`. Live: one tab set Shell commands to Never; the
other, still showing Ask me, was refused and then showed Never (capture 04).

## FIXED-809 — A task sent twice was filed twice

**Severity: Medium. Area: Tasks / API. Status: Fixed 2026-10-05. §13.2 item 6's
owner-scoped, payload-bound idempotency keys.**

**Fixed.** `POST /api/tasks` accepts `Idempotency-Key` (migration RAIKER-2094,
`idempotency_keys`, kept 24 hours). The same owner, key and body get the first
answer again; the same key on a changed body is `409 idempotency_key_reused`;
a key still in flight is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`; a refused request
releases its key so the corrected draft can go. The Tasks composer and Build's
agent form hold one key per draft until the server accepts it, so a double
click or a resend after a lost response files once.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_idempotency_keys.py`. Live: the same draft sent twice
returned one task id and the queue held one card; a changed resend was refused

## FIXED-810 — Cached prompt tokens were recorded as zero and priced as nothing

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / usage and cost. Status: Fixed 2026-10-05 —
found by this round's cost-limited routine.**

**Observed.** An Anthropic routine wrote 7,976 tokens to the prompt cache on
its first call and read them on each of the next three; the cost limit saw a
fraction of the bill and let it run four calls.

**Root cause.** The orchestrator records `summarize_model_usage`'s normalised
keys (`cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`), and `ModelUsageLedger.record`
read only the raw Anthropic spelling — so every cached token in the usage
ledger was zero — and `UsageTotals.cost` priced input and output only. Every
conversation and provider cost the Models and Chat pages showed under-stated a
cached prompt.

**Fixed.** The ledger reads both spellings; `UsageTotals.cost` includes cache
writes and reads at their own rates; the cost meter reads the normalised keys.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_cost_accounting.py`
(*TestCachedTokensAreCounted*); the orchestrator cost tests use a cached
response.

## FIXED-811 — A profile's stated cache rates were dropped

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / pricing. Status: Fixed 2026-10-05 — found by
this round.**

**Observed.** After FIXED-810, the routine's spend came to $0.0178 for two
calls instead of $0.0126.

**Root cause.** `price_from_config` read `input` and `output` and ignored the
`cache_write` and `cache_read` rates the Anthropic profile states per model
precisely so nothing has to infer them; cached tokens fell back to the input
rate — a cache read at ten times its bill.

**Fixed.** Both rates are read. **Evidence.**
`test_a_profiles_stated_cache_rates_are_read`. Live: the next run's first call
cost $0.0108 (353 in, 8,119 cache-write, 67 out) and it was stopped there.

## FIXED-812 — A damaged database read as the machine's memory, or as a generic failure

**Severity: Medium. Area: Storage / lock screen. Status: Fixed 2026-10-05 —
found by this round's lock-screen phase.**

**Observed.** The round damaged a database's first pages with the host
stopped. The lock screen said *This machine would not give SQLCipher the memory
it needs* — the wrong diagnosis, with no backup offered. Without memory
security the same file read as `store_open_failed`.

**Root cause.** Once a host had run against it, the damaged file's first page
still decrypted, so the key check passed and the failure came later in
bootstrap: *database disk image is malformed*, or — with memory security on —
the `MemoryError` SQLCipher raises for a page it cannot decrypt, which
`store_health` labels a memory-lock refusal.

**Fixed.** A `DatabaseError` naming damage, or a `MemoryError` while a scratch
encrypted store opens in the same process, is `store_unreadable` from
bootstrap and from the connection's memory retry; every cached handle to the
file is retired. A real memory refusal — the scratch store failing too — is
still named as one.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_lock_screen_recovery.py` (both paths, and the
machine case). Live: the same workspace then read `store_unreadable` and was
restored from the lock screen (captures 10–11).

## FIXED-813 — An MCP tool was accepted as the server declared it at the click, not as the owner read it

**Severity: High. Area: MCP / authority. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. §13.2 item 6
and DEC-15 step 10.**

**Observed.** Accepting a held tool sent only its name; the server accepted it
"as declared now". A server re-lists its tools on every session, so a tool
reworded between the card rendering and the click — *Delete one draft* becoming
*Delete every note you have* — was accepted in words nobody read.

**Fixed.** Each held tool carries the fingerprint of the declaration the card
shows (`PendingTool.fingerprint`), and Accept sends it back
(`ApproveMcpToolsRequest.fingerprints`). When any named tool no longer matches,
nothing is accepted: `409 mcp_tool_changed`. The page re-reads the card, shows
the server's new sentence and says *changed how it describes that tool since
this page showed it, so nothing was accepted*. Clients that send no fingerprint
behave as before.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_mcp_tool_review.py::test_acceptance_is_of_the_declaration_the_owner_read`;
`McpView.test.ts` (2). Live: capture
[07](../screenshots/2026-10-10-revisions-round/07-mcp-tool-changed-not-accepted.png).

## FIXED-815 — A stale Messaging tab could re-admit a sender removed in another

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. §13.2 item 6 for
channel configuration.**

**Observed.** Enable, senders, routing, destination and unpair saved whatever
the page held. A tab opened before a sender was removed saved the old allowlist
back — the one list the receiver enforces — and said nothing.

**Fixed.** Each pairing carries a revision (`raiker/channels/revision.py`, a
digest of its owner-decided fields) on its profile; every change sends it as
`expected_revision`, and a pairing changed since is `409 channel_conflict` with
nothing written. Each answer carries the new revision. Messaging says *This
channel was changed somewhere else since this page loaded, so nothing was
changed* and shows the current settings.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_owner_surface.py` (service and route);
`MessagingView.test.ts`. Live: two tabs — one removed `oncall`, the other's
save of `oncall, ops` was refused and the stored list stayed `ops` (capture
[04](../screenshots/2026-10-10-revisions-round/04-channel-stale-tab-refused.png)).

## FIXED-817 — A channel could only be on or off; there was no way to contain it and keep its evidence

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-14 step 10.**

**Observed.** Turning a channel off refuses messages outright, so containing a
channel that was misbehaving lost what arrived while it was contained.

**Fixed.** **Pause** (`PUT /api/channels/pairings/{id}/paused`, migration
RAIKER-2096) is a third state. An allowlisted message is still checked
(allowlist, budget, loop guard) and recorded — receipt and redacted preview,

## FIXED-820 — Updates listed recovery points without saying whether they could open this data

**Severity: Medium. Area: Updates. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-21 Updates
row's schema compatibility.**

**Observed.** A recovery point was a version number. An older build refuses a
database a newer one shaped (FIXED-803), so rolling back past a migration left
the workspace locked — and the page offering the point said nothing.

**Fixed.** A release records the schema generation it opens in
`installation.json`; each recovery point reports it, and `GET /api/host/update`
adds this workspace's generation and, per point, `opens_this_workspace`
(true / false / unknown for a build that recorded none). Updates says *can open
this workspace's data*, *would refuse … roll back only with a backup taken
before that update*, or *not known*, and the offered-update text says the
database is backed up before it migrates.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_api_updates.py` (2); `Updates.test.ts`. Live: capture

## FIXED-821 — A backup's rows pointed at checkpoint files and uploads it did not hold

**Severity: Medium. Area: Storage / backups. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-24
step 5's "referenced blobs".**

**Observed.** Backups held the database and memory files; checkpoint
pre-images (`.raiker/checkpoints`) and knowledge uploads (`.raiker/artifacts`)
were listed as not included, so a restored workspace offered checkpoints and
sources it could not deliver.

**Fixed.** Both trees are copied with every backup (regular files only), and
the manifest records each one's file count, size and a digest over every file,
which **Verify** recomputes — a changed file is *Damaged*. A restore into a new
folder carries them; the lock screen's in-place restore adds back only files
the workspace lost and replaces none (checkpoint objects are named by their own
hash; an upload present is newer). Only the database is encrypted; the page
says the files are copied as the workspace keeps them. Not included now: the
audit log and attached folders.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_workspace_backups.py` (3); `BackupsCard.test.ts`.
Live: capture [09](../screenshots/2026-10-10-revisions-round/09-backup-carries-files.png)
(*1 checkpoint file · 1 upload*).

## FIXED-822 — A release published no SBOM and nothing bound its artifacts to their inputs

**Severity: Medium. Area: Release / supply chain. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10.
DEC-17 step 10, DEC-24 step 7 (SBOM bound to artifact digests), CI-03, REL-03.**

**Observed.** Licensing generated an SPDX SBOM and discarded it; a release
published artifacts and a signed channel index, and nothing tied an installer
to the commit, the dependency lock or an SBOM.

**Fixed.** `raiker-release provenance` writes `SHA256SUMS` and
`release-provenance.json` — version, channel, source commit, workflow run, the
SHA-256 of `uv.lock`, of the SBOM and of every artifact — signed with the
release key (`.sig`). `raiker-release verify` checks the signature and every
digest whenever the record is present. The release workflow's channel job
generates `raiker-<version>.spdx.json`, binds it, and publishes all of it
beside the installers; Licensing keeps its SBOM as a run artifact. This is a
signed binding, not SLSA attestation.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_release_pipeline.py::test_a_release_carries_a_signed_provenance_record_and_checksums`
(a swapped SBOM is refused); `tests/test_release_workflow.py`. The release
workflow is manual and was not run in this round.

by file, line, rule and a fingerprint — never the value. A deliberate fixture is

test fixtures (all fake) are listed, expiring 2027-04-10.

passing its own scan.

## FIXED-825 — A routine a stopped host left running never ran again

**Severity: High. Area: Tasks / scheduler. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10 — found
writing DEC-24 step 3's recovery matrix.**

**Observed.** A scheduled run is claimed `queued → running` and awaited in the
host process. A host stopped mid-run left the row `running` with nothing
advancing it, and only `queued` work is ever claimed — so a routine in that
state never ran again, and its card went on saying it was running.

**Fixed.** At start, before the first tick, `TaskScheduler.settle_interrupted_runs`
settles every task left `running` or `continuing` as a run that did not
complete — *Raiker stopped while this run was in progress … It was not run
again on its own* — never retried, since what it did is unknown. A routine
moves to its next slot as any failed cycle does (and counts towards the
three-failure pause); one being cancelled is cancelled.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_task_scheduler.py::test_a_run_the_host_stopped_in_the_middle_of_is_settled_not_left_running`.
Live: a routine left `running`, the host restarted, and it read `queued` for
2026-10-11 07:00 with the statement in its history (capture
[14](../screenshots/2026-10-10-revisions-round/14-interrupted-run-settled.png)).

## FIXED-828 — An update could start on a disk it would fill

**Severity: Medium. Area: Updates / installer. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10.
DEC-17 step 7's "check free space".**

**Observed.** `apply_signed_update` extracted the bundle beside the
installation and copied the running version to its recovery point without
asking whether the volume could hold both. A full disk part-way through left a
half-written staging tree, and a disk filled by an update is a host that cannot
write its own database afterwards.

**Fixed.** Before the first write the update adds what the archive unpacks to
and what the recovery copy needs, per volume, plus 64 MiB of headroom, and is
refused `update_insufficient_space` when the volume cannot hold it. zipfile
stops an entry at its declared size and fails its CRC if the data runs on, so an
archive that lies about its sizes cannot outgrow the check.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_signed_updates.py::test_an_update_the_disk_cannot_hold_is_refused_before_the_first_write`,
`::test_the_space_check_counts_the_staged_tree_and_the_recovery_copy`,
`::test_an_entry_that_unpacks_larger_than_it_declared_is_refused`.

## FIXED-829 — A swapped installation was never checked before the old one was thrown away

**Severity: Medium. Area: Updates / installer. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10.
DEC-17 step 7's "health-check and roll back on failure".**

**Observed.** The final step of an update was two renames, after which the
previous tree was deleted. Nothing read the live path to confirm it was the
release the signed manifest named, so a bundle whose contents disagreed with its
manifest was installed and discovered at the next start.

**Fixed.** After the swap `installed_tree_healthy` reads the live
`version.txt` (and `installation.json` where the build wrote one) against the
manifest's version. A tree that fails — or a check that raises — is moved out,
the previous version renamed back, and the update refused
`update_health_check_failed`; `raiker-app update` says the previous version was
put back. A rollback that itself cannot complete is
`update_health_check_failed_rollback_incomplete`, and the command names the
`--rollback` that restores the retained copy.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_signed_updates.py::test_a_swapped_tree_that_fails_its_health_check_is_rolled_back`,
`::test_a_check_that_raises_counts_as_failed`,
`::test_the_default_check_reads_the_version_the_manifest_named`.

## FIXED-830 — A failed update left a recovery copy that refused the next attempt

**Severity: Medium. Area: Updates / installer. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10 —
found writing FIXED-829.**

**Observed.** The running version is copied to `recovery/<version>` before a
migration runs. When the migration (or the swap) failed, the copy stayed, and
the owner's next attempt was refused `recovery_point_already_exists` — an
update that failed once could never be retried without deleting a directory by
hand.

**Fixed.** A recovery copy made for an update that did not happen is removed
with the staging tree on every failure path: preparation, the swap and the
health check.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_signed_updates.py::test_a_failed_migration_leaves_no_recovery_copy_to_block_a_retry`;
the health-check test above installs the same bundle on its second attempt.

## FIXED-831 — An update could install a build that would refuse the workspace's data

**Severity: Medium. Area: Updates / installer. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10.
DEC-17 step 7's "check compatibility".**

**Observed.** A build refuses a database a newer build shaped
(`store_schema_newer`, FIXED-803), and each release records the schema
generation it opens (FIXED-820). The updater read neither, so a release built
before the workspace's last migration was installed and then refused the data
at start.

**Fixed.** `download_and_apply` reads the workspace's generation
(`workspace_schema_generation`, shared with the Updates page) and
`apply_signed_update` compares it with the staged build's recorded generation
before anything moves: an older one is refused `update_schema_incompatible`.
A build that records none, or a database that could not be read, is not
refused for it — unknown is not incompatible.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_signed_updates.py::test_a_release_that_cannot_open_this_workspace_is_refused_before_anything_moves`
and `::test_a_release_that_opens_it_or_an_unknown_reading_is_not_refused` (3).

## FIXED-832 — Updates offered a release without saying how large it was or what it changed

**Severity: Low. Area: Settings / Updates. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-21
Updates row's "download size … notes".**

**Fixed.** The signed channel index carries each artifact's `size` and the
release's `notes` (at most 4,000 characters, from the release workflow's new
`notes` input, passed through the environment so the text cannot become shell).
Settings → Updates shows *Download size* and *What this release changes*, or
says a release published before either was recorded does not state them. The
size is also the most a download reads: the updater fetches no more than the
signed index says, instead of the 512 MiB ceiling. An index with a malformed
size or note, or a field it does not know, is refused.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_signed_updates.py` (size/notes parse, refusals,
bounded download), `tests/test_release_pipeline.py::test_the_channel_index_carries_bounded_release_notes`;
`Updates.test.ts` (2).

## FIXED-833 — A worker whose run was settled under it could still write its outcome

**Severity: Medium. Area: Tasks / scheduler. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-12
step 4's fencing token; §13.2 item 7's "fence stale workers".**

**Observed.** A scheduled run's claim was a status change and nothing else.
When a host settled a run it believed abandoned (FIXED-825) while another host
on the same workspace was still on it, both wrote the outcome — the second
overwriting the first, and a routine possibly re-armed twice.

**Fixed.** Each claim takes the next `claim_generation` (migration
RAIKER-2098), and the worker holds the generation it was claimed at. Settling
is one compare-and-swap (`fence_task_claim`): whoever moves the generation on
settles, and a worker whose claim was taken records nothing and logs that it
did not. Restart settlement and a skipped missed slot take the claim the same
way.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_task_scheduler.py` (5): each claim takes the next
generation; only the current holder settles; a worker whose run was settled
under it records nothing; the holder lands its outcome; a settle that lost the
race leaves the run to its worker.

## FIXED-834 — A plugin update that asked for more was installed like the first install

**Severity: Medium. Area: Extensions / plugins. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10.
DEC-15 step 10's "updates show a permission diff and require review when
authority grows".**

**Observed.** Installing a new version of an installed plugin wrote a new
install record with whatever permissions the manifest asked for. The plan the
owner read listed the permissions, not what had changed, so a version that grew
its authority looked the same as one that did not.

**Fixed.** `/plugin-plan` reads an update against the installed version —
`updates_installed_version`, `permissions_added`, `permissions_removed` — and
says when it asks for more. The install executor refuses such an update
`plugin_permissions_grew_unreviewed`, naming what it adds, unless the owner
accepted **exactly** the permission set the manifest now asks for
(`--install --accept-permissions`); a manifest changed between the plan and the
install asks again. An update that asks for the same or less installs as
before; every install's result carries the diff.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_phase_4_plugin_install_runtime.py` (3): held until the
exact set is accepted (a different set refused); a narrower update installs
without a second question; the plan reads the update against what is installed.

## FIXED-835 — No static analysis for security ran on any change

**Severity: Medium. Area: CI / supply chain. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-24
step 7's "SAST gate with triage owner, exceptions, expiry".**

**Fixed.** `scripts/scan_sast.py` runs ruff's Bandit rules (`S`) over
`raiker`, `apps` and `scripts` on every change, in CI beside the credential
scan. Style-only rules (`assert`, `try/except/pass`, "a subprocess was
started") are not gated. Each of the 112 current findings — SQL composed from
in-code fragments with every value bound, constants that name environment
variables, sandbox-only paths, a capability flag named `shell` — was read and
is an entry in `.github/sast-exceptions.json` with an owner, a reason and an
expiry. An expired or unused entry fails the check; the fingerprint is the rule
and the flagged source, so moving code keeps a review and changing it asks
again. Two SHA-1 uses that are not security hashes are now marked

## FIXED-836 — A UTF-16 document part could carry the DTD the attachment check refuses

**Severity: Medium. Area: Attachments. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10 — found triaging
FIXED-835's XML findings.**

**Observed.** A `.docx`/`.xlsx` part is refused when it carries `<!DOCTYPE`,
the only way to declare the entities behind a billion-laughs expansion. The
check was a UTF-8 byte scan, and the parser also reads UTF-16 parts, where the
same declaration is two bytes a character: a UTF-16 part with a DTD passed the
check and reached the parser.

**Fixed.** The declaration is looked for in UTF-8, UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_document_attachments.py::test_a_utf16_docx_with_doctype_fails_closed`
(3 encodings) — all three failed before the change.

## FIXED-840 — Nothing bounded what the owner's models spent in total

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / runtime. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10. DEC-24
step 2's budget across foreground turns, tasks and children.**

**Observed.** A routine run had its own cost limit (FIXED-804), and each
provider an advisory weekly token budget nothing read. A dozen routines each
inside their limits, a long Build session and the work they delegated could
together spend whatever the providers would bill.

**Fixed.** One owner-wide spending limit for the last 24 hours (migration
RAIKER-2099; `GET`/`PUT /api/models/spend-limit`), shown and set on Models →
Usage with what the window has spent. It is read at every turn's safe boundary
before each model call — the boundary Stop and a run's own limit use — from the
usage ledger every surface writes, priced at read time with the rate Models
shows. A turn that starts over it stops before its first model call; one that
crosses it stops before its next, so the overrun is the responses in flight.
Usage on a model with no known price is named, not counted as free. The weekly
token budgets stay advisory and say so by contrast.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_tool_call_loop.py` (5): stopped before the next
call with `turn_spend_limit_reached`; a turn started over the limit never asks
the model; no limit stops nothing; the window counts priced usage and names
unpriced models; bounds. `ProviderUsagePanel.test.ts` (3). Live, real OpenRouter
GPT-4o Mini turns: $0.0014 of $0.01 (capture
[01](../screenshots/2026-10-10-spend-limit-round/01-spend-limit-set.png)); at
$0.0101 the next turn stopped with the limit named and the spend unchanged
([02](../screenshots/2026-10-10-spend-limit-round/02-turn-stopped-by-spend-limit.png),
[03](../screenshots/2026-10-10-spend-limit-round/03-spend-limit-reached.png));
cleared, the next turn answered.

## FIXED-841 — A streamed OpenRouter turn recorded no usage, so every cost limit read it as free

**Severity: High. Area: Models / providers. Status: Fixed 2026-10-10 — found by
the live round for FIXED-840.**

**Observed.** A real OpenRouter turn answered and the usage ledger stayed
empty: Usage showed zero tokens and the spending window $0.0000. Two causes.
OpenRouter streams were never asked for usage (`stream_options` was sent only
to OpenAI and Ollama), and a usage block that arrives on the same chunk as the
last choice — OpenRouter's shape — was discarded, because usage was read only
from a chunk with no choices.

**Effect.** Every OpenRouter turn was invisible to the per-run cost limit
(FIXED-804), the new owner-wide limit, Models → Usage and the per-turn token
count.

**Fixed.** OpenRouter streams ask for usage, and a usage block is kept wherever
it appears; the consumer keeps the last, so a server repeating cumulative usage
counts once.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_provider_contract_regressions.py::test_a_usage_block_on_the_last_choice_chunk_is_kept`,
`::test_openrouter_streams_ask_for_usage`. Live: after the fix the same turn
recorded $0.0014 and the limit above was reached by real spend.

## FIXED-844 — A re-sent channel update was a second message and started a second turn

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 4's
provider event id and idempotency result.**

**Observed.** Telegram re-sends an update it got no 2xx for, and a routed turn
can outlast its patience. Nothing kept the provider's `update_id`, so each
re-send was accepted as a new message, spent the sender's budget again, counted
towards the loop guard, and — on a `new_turn` route — started a second turn.

**Fixed.** The Telegram adapter carries `update_id`; the generic webhook takes
an optional `Idempotency-Key` (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{8,128}`, else 422
`idempotency_key_invalid`). Once the sender is known to be allowed, the event
is claimed in `channel_inbound_events` (migration RAIKER-2100, keyed by
connector and event, kept 48 hours) before any budget is spent. A repeat is
answered 200 with the **first** message's receipt id and conversation,
`reason_code: duplicate_event`, recorded in the audit log and given no second
receipt. A message refused by a budget or the loop guard gives its claim back,
so the provider's retry is a fresh try.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_inbound_dedup.py` (7 for this entry). Live:
the same Telegram update posted three times returned one receipt id, the second
and third `duplicate_event`; a new `update_id` with the same words was a new
message; Messaging's recent activity listed two messages, not four. The webhook
with one `Idempotency-Key` sent twice answered the first id, and `a b` was 422.

## FIXED-845 — A channel's inbound budget was per sender only

**Severity: Low. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 8's
per-sender/channel/global limits.**

**Observed.** BUG-225's budget bounded each allowlisted sender, and nothing
bounded a channel with many senders (a group) or the host across channels.

**Fixed.** Two more windows sit behind the sender's: one per channel
(`RAIKER_CHANNEL_INBOUND_CHANNEL_RATE`, default four times the sender's) and
one for the host (`RAIKER_CHANNEL_INBOUND_GLOBAL_RATE`, default ten times). The
smallest scope is checked first and nothing is spent unless all three have
room, so a flood from others never uses up a quiet sender's budget. Refusals
are 429 `channel_rate_limited` / `inbound_rate_limited`, recorded with their
limit; Messaging words both. The approval relay uses the same budgets.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_inbound_dedup.py` (4 for this entry),
`channelSetup.test.ts`.

## FIXED-846 — A channel went on with a destination nobody had tested

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 3:

operating system calls *available* (Windows `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, Linux
`MemAvailable`), `low` under 512 MB or 5%, `critical` under 256 MB or 2%, and

## FIXED-848 — Container base images were never scanned, and neither pinned base could still be pulled (was BUG-329)

**Severity: Medium. Area: CI / containers. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. The rest of
DEC-24 step 7 after FIXED-837.**

**Observed.** FIXED-837 checked how the sandbox and egress-proxy images are
built, not what they are built on. Pointing a scanner at the two pinned bases
found that the registry no longer serves either digest
(`MANIFEST_UNKNOWN`): neither image could have been rebuilt.

**Fixed.** Both bases are re-pinned to the current `python:3.13.16-slim` and
`-alpine` digests, and the sandbox's `# syntax=` frontend is pinned too
(FIXED-863). `scripts/scan_images.py` scans every pinned `FROM` image with
grype straight from the registry and fails a fixable High or Critical finding
unless `.github/image-scan-exceptions.json` holds a reviewed, unexpired entry;
an expired or unused entry fails too. CI's **Container image vulnerabilities**

SHA-256 before running it — the scanner's own release channel is supply-chain
input. One exception is recorded: zlib CVE-2026-85091 in the Alpine base, fixed
upstream in 1.3.2-r1 but not yet in the image, expiring 2026-11-10.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_scan_images.py` (8). Run against the real registry:

## FIXED-849 — A scheduled run had no lease, so one nobody was working on stayed running

**Severity: Medium. Area: Tasks. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-12 step 4's
heartbeat, after FIXED-833's fencing token.**

**Observed.** A claim was fenced but had no lease. A run whose worker died
without settling — a coroutine that never returned, a second host that went
away — stayed `running` until the next restart.

**Fixed.** A claim starts a lease (`run_heartbeat_at`, migration RAIKER-2101);
the worker renews it every 30 seconds under its claim generation. Each
scheduler pass settles a run unrenewed for five minutes as not finished — not
retried, as a restart settles it — and a worker that finds its claim taken when
it renews asks its turn to stop. The recovery matrix says so.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_task_scheduler.py` (5 for this entry).

## FIXED-850 — A long routine held up every other background pass

**Severity: Medium. Area: Host / Observability. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11.
DEC-24 step 1's "give each worker bounded queues, watchdogs" — found writing
FIXED-849.**

**Observed.** The host tick awaited the scheduled-work pass, and one run may
last an hour. For that hour approved work did not continue, no search index
was checked and no local model was watched; after five minutes each of those
passes read *not running* on *Needs your attention*.

**Fixed.** The scheduled-work pass runs beside the tick as its own task, one at
a time; while it is busy each tick records it alive, and FIXED-849's lease is
what notices a run that has stopped.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_due_work_beside_the_tick.py` (2). Live: every
background pass read `ok` on the diagnostics read.

## FIXED-854 — An enforcing hook that crashed or timed out let the action through

**Severity: High. Area: Hooks / governance. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-23
step 4: "optional observer failure can continue; required enforcement failure
stops".**

**Observed.** A hook the owner gave decision authority — a built-in check, or
a command or `http` handler with `decision_authority` — that timed out or
errored was recorded and skipped, so the guard let through exactly what it was
there to stop.

**Fixed.** Its failure now counts as **ask**: the action goes to the owner for
a decision. A hook without authority is an observer and still only records its
failure. A deny from another hook still wins. `hook_timeout` / `hook_failed`
say `failed_closed`, and the Hooks tab's line says *sent to you for a
decision*.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_hook_fail_closed.py` (5).

## FIXED-855 — A delivery Raiker sent over a channel left no record

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 7:
"create outbound delivery records before send".**

**Observed.** Only an owner's test left a receipt, written after it had
settled; a real reply or notice sent over a paired channel left none, so
Messaging could say what arrived and never what went out.

**Fixed.** The channel executor writes the receipt — keyed by the governed
action's id — as *queued* before anything is sent and settles it *delivered* or
*failed* with the reason on every path (paused, too long, adapter refusal,
egress, destination error). A test is a `test_delivery`; anything else a
`message`, shown as *Raiker sent a message*. A test refused before the executor
(a closed gate) still gets its receipt from the control service.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_outbound_receipts.py` (4),
`channelSetup.test.ts`. Live: the webhook's test receipt read *queued →
delivered* ([05](../screenshots/2026-10-11-channels-runtime-round/05-webhook-tested-then-on.png)).

## FIXED-857 — A configured runtime could not be turned off, and off would not have stopped its commands

**Severity: Medium. Area: Runtime / Settings. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-11
step 6: "disabling a runtime stops new claims, requests bounded cancellation for

**Fixed.** `PUT /api/execution-environments/{profile_id}/enabled` turns a
configured SSH, Daytona or container target off or on. Off stops new work
(resolution already refused a disabled profile and never fell back to the

on*.

## FIXED-864 — A local MCP server could only be given a secret by giving it to every local server

**Severity: Medium. Area: MCP / secrets. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-15 step 2: "replace inline secrets with purpose-bound secret handles; deliver only declared values to that server process and redact before persistence/model exposure".**

**Observed.** The one way to hand a local server a credential was `RAIKER_MCP_ENV_ALLOWLIST`: a name there is passed from Raiker's own environment to *every* local MCP server, so a weather server's key was in the environment of all of them, and the value had to live in the environment Raiker was started with.

**Fixed.** `raiker/runtime/mcp_secrets.py`. A secret is a variable name the owner gives one local server, its value in the encrypted connector vault under that server's id (`mcp_server_env:<server_id>`). `_run_session` adds it to that server's constructed environment and no other, and replaces each value in what the server writes back before anything reads it. Names that the launcher sets (`PATH`, `HOME`, …) or that configure the boundary are refused (`mcp_secret_name_reserved`); a remote server is refused (`mcp_secret_local_only`); removing the server removes its secrets. `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id}/secrets[/{name}]` return names only, and the server list carries them as `vault_env` (a key the response redactor does not mistake for a secret). Extensions → MCP has **Secrets for this server** with a password field, and *What it can reach* names them as this server's only. Events `mcp_server_secret_set` / `_removed` carry the name, never the value.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_mcp_server_secrets.py` (7 — a real local server sees its own secret and another server does not; a server that echoes its token hands back `[REDACTED_SECRET]`), three contract cases, `McpView.test.ts`. ## FIXED-865 — A configured runtime could be turned off but never removed

**Severity: Low. Area: Runtime / Settings. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-11 step 6: "deletion requires no active references or an explicit migration choice".**

**Observed.** FIXED-857 added Turn off; a target the owner was done with stayed on Settings → Runtime for good, and nothing said what removing one would need.

**Fixed.** `DELETE /api/execution-environments/{profile_id}`. Refused `409 execution_environment_in_use` with the count while commands run there (turning it off stops them first); refused `execution_environment_selected` when it is where work runs by default unless `move_to` names a ready replacement, which is selected before anything is removed. Only the profile row goes; command runs and cloud cost stay as evidence. Runtime has **Remove** on configured targets; for the default one the confirm names where work will run instead.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_execution_environment_remove.py` (5), a contract case, `Runtime.test.ts` (3). Live: an SSH target added through the form and removed — *Build host was removed.* ([05](../screenshots/2026-10-11-review-steps-round/05-runtime-target-removed.png)).

## FIXED-866 — A delivered message had no reference to what the platform accepted

**Severity: Low. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 7: "update attempts, provider IDs, delivered/failed state".**

**Observed.** A receipt said *delivered* and nothing tied it to the message on the platform: Telegram answers with a `message_id`, a receiver may answer with its own id, and both were read and dropped.

**Fixed.** Each adapter reads one id out of the platform's answer (`provider_message_id`: Telegram's `result.message_id`, a webhook's `id` or `message_id`), short and plain or nothing; the rest of the body is dropped where it is read (`post_url(..., keep_body=True)`). The receipt keeps it (migration RAIKER-2103) and Messaging says *Delivered · the channel's id for it is …*.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_delivery_review.py`, `channelSetup.test.ts`. Live: a test to a local receiver read *Delivered · the channel's id for it is rcv-0001* ([03](../screenshots/2026-10-11-review-steps-round/03-delivery-id-and-review-list.png)).

## FIXED-867 — A delivery that failed was a line in recent activity and nothing asked anyone to look

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 7: "dead-letter review independently from task status".**

**Observed.** A failed delivery was one of the last five receipts on its channel and scrolled away with the next message; nothing collected what had not arrived or let the owner say they had dealt with it.

**Fixed.** Each channel lists **Deliveries to review** — outbound receipts that failed or whose outcome is unknown and are not yet reviewed — with the reason and what to do about it (fix it and resend from whatever asked, or check the channel before resending). **Mark reviewed** (`POST /api/channels/deliveries/{receipt_id}/reviewed`, event `channel_delivery_reviewed`) takes one off the list and changes nothing else; nothing is ever sent again on its own. The list is also an item on Home's attention feed (FIXED-873).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_delivery_review.py` (6), a contract case, `MessagingView.test.ts`. Live: a test refused by the closed capability on the list, then marked reviewed — off the list, still *failed* in the record, gone from Home ([03](../screenshots/2026-10-11-review-steps-round/03-delivery-id-and-review-list.png), [04](../screenshots/2026-10-11-review-steps-round/04-delivery-marked-reviewed.png)); at 390 wide, dark ([09](../screenshots/2026-10-11-review-steps-round/09-messaging-review-390-dark.png)).

## FIXED-868 — A delivery a stopped host was in the middle of stayed queued for ever

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging / recovery. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. §13.2 item 7: "represent outcome_unknown, reconcile, then obtain an explicit retry decision".**

**Observed.** The receipt is written *queued* before send (FIXED-855) and settled in the same process. A host stopped between the two left it *queued* — *Sending* on the page — with nothing ever settling it, though it may well have arrived.

**Fixed.** At start, beside the task-run settlement, `settle_unsettled_outbound_receipts` marks every outbound receipt still queued as `outcome_unknown_at` with `delivery_outcome_unknown`. It is put on the channel's review list as *Outcome unknown — Raiker stopped while sending it. It was not sent again.* The recovery matrix's channel row says so.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_delivery_review.py` (2), `test_recovery_matrix`. ## FIXED-869 — A webhook delivery carried nothing a receiver could deduplicate by

**Severity: Low. Area: Messaging. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-12 step 4: "reuse its idempotency key where the destination supports it".**

**Observed.** A webhook delivery had no stable identity, so a copy a proxy or a deliberate resend produced was a second message to the receiver.

**Fixed.** A webhook delivery carries its receipt id as `Idempotency-Key` and in the signed body as `delivery_id`. Telegram's Bot API takes no such key, which is why an unknown outcome is reviewed rather than resent (FIXED-868).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_delivery_review.py`. Live: the receiver logged `Idempotency-Key: act_ace021…`, the receipt's own id.

## FIXED-870 — A memory the owner forgot could be proposed or written straight back

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. §13.2 item 4: "Forget … records a suppression tombstone so the same source does not silently re-create it".**

**Observed.** Forget kept a content-free tombstone with the record's checksum and nothing compared new writes against it: the next turn that said the same sentence was proposed again, and the memory tool could write it back outright.

**Fixed.** `memory_text_forgotten` compares a sentence's checksum with the owner's forgotten records. A completed turn's proposals skip it (counted as `suppressed` on `memory_relationship_extraction_completed`), and the memory tool refuses it (`memory_forgotten_by_owner`). The owner adding it again on Memory is the explicit restore, and lifts the suppression. Forget's confirmation now says so.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_forget_suppression.py` (6). Live: *Rahul prefers tea* approved, forgotten from the card's **More**, then sent in a new conversation — `/api/memory/proposals` stayed empty and Home showed no proposal.

## FIXED-871 — A Retry was a new turn that nothing linked to the one it repeated

**Severity: Low. Area: Chat / Build. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-22 step 3: "retry creates a new attempt linked to its source".**

**Observed.** **Retry** sent the same words as an unrelated turn; a reopened conversation showed two requests where there had been one asked twice.

**Fixed.** Chat and Build send `retry_of_turn_id`; the server checks it is a turn of the same conversation before anything is bound or written (`422 retry_source_not_in_session`) and records the link in `turn_retries` (migration RAIKER-2104). Every read of the conversation carries it, and the retry says *Retry of an earlier turn — that turn is kept as it was*, linking back.

## FIXED-872 — A streamed answer the owner stopped was billed and counted as free

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / usage. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-24 step 2: "account for cancelled calls that a provider still bills".**

**Observed.** Stopping a streamed turn returned before the usage ledger was written, and Anthropic's input count arrived only with the closing event, so a stopped turn — whose input and partial output the provider bills — read as nothing to every spending limit.

**Fixed.** Anthropic's stream passes on the input usage as soon as `message_start` reports it; the closing event supersedes it. A stopped stream, or one that fails mid-way, records whatever the provider had counted. A provider that reports usage only at the end has said nothing yet, and nothing is invented for it (BUG-333).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_stopped_stream_usage.py` (2; the first fails without the fix), `test_prompt_cache_metrics.py`. Not reachable live this round: the identity-linked Anthropic key could not be used (BUG-332) and the stand-in speaks the OpenAI-compatible stream.

## FIXED-873 — Home's attention rail could see three subsystems and nothing else that waited on the owner

**Severity: Medium. Area: Home / navigation. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-02 steps 2, 4 and 5: a server-backed Needs-attention feed with stable ids, severity, reason, origin, action and time, resolved only by the authoritative subsystem.**

**Observed.** Home assembled *Needs your attention* in the browser from approvals, readiness and blocked tasks. A proposed memory, a delivery to review, an MCP tool held for review or a containment signal waited on its own page.

**Fixed.** `GET /api/attention` (`raiker/control/dashboard_parts/attention.py`) reads each subsystem's own record on every call — security signals, approvals, blocked tasks, memory proposals, deliveries to review, held MCP tools — and returns items by reference (id, severity, title, reason, origin, the one action, since), containment first. An item disappears when its subsystem says it is resolved; a subsystem that cannot be read is listed in `unknown`, never counted as clear. Home renders the items its tiles do not already cover and withholds the all-clear while anything is unread.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_attention_feed.py` (5), a contract case, `WorkbenchView.test.ts` (2). ## FIXED-874 — Nothing said which memories most needed the owner's look, or why

**Severity: Low. Area: Memory. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-13 step 3: "review priority from retention, sensitivity, use, verification, conflict, provenance and pin — not one opaque score".**

**Observed.** Retention (FIXED-689) counted records one policy at a time; nothing ordered the set by what most needed review or said why a record was there.

**Fixed.** `raiker/memory/review_priority.py` names each factor — expired or expiring, personal or unclassified sensitivity, written by Raiker and never edited, low confidence, replaced another, stale or never recalled — with a fixed weight; the priority is their sum, and a pin lowers it by one without exempting anything. Each memory carries `review_priority` and `review_reasons`. ## FIXED-875 — A late stop or steer was applied as though it were the newest

**Severity: Low. Area: Chat / Build. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-22 steps 1–2: "serialize control decisions per session and reject stale commands".**

**Observed.** `/api/interrupts` applied stop and steer in arrival order, so a steer delayed behind a later stop — or a retransmission of one already applied — was applied again as new.

**Fixed.** A command may carry `client_id` and `client_sequence`; the server keeps each client's last number per conversation (migration RAIKER-2105, one write transaction). An older one is refused `409 control_command_stale` with nothing applied; the same command under the same number is answered `duplicate: true` and applied once; half a pair is `422`. The web client numbers every stop and steer per tab. A client that sends neither is ordered by arrival, as before.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_control_command_sequence.py` (9), `controlSequence.test.ts`. Live, from the signed-in page: stop #2 applied, steer #1 refused 409, steer #3 queued, steer #3 again answered as a duplicate.

## FIXED-876 — A webhook message carried its secret on the wire and could be replayed for ever

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging / security. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11. DEC-14 step 5: "verify signature, timestamp/nonce, account and pairing before routing".**

**Observed.** The reference webhook took the shared inbound secret in a header: every message carried it, and anyone who saw one request could replay it indefinitely.

**Fixed.** A sender may sign instead: `X-Raiker-Timestamp` and `X-Raiker-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of "<timestamp>.<body>">`, keyed by the inbound secret, which then never travels. Checked before routing; refused `channel_signature_invalid` or, beyond five minutes either way, `channel_signature_expired`; the signature is then claimed once like a provider event id, so a replay is a repeat. `RAIKER_CHANNEL_INBOUND_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE` refuses an unsigned message (`channel_signature_required`). Messaging's posture lists **Signed messages · Accepted / Required**.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_inbound_signature.py` (9), `MessagingView.test.ts`. Live, against the running host: signed → 200; the same bytes again → the first message's id with `duplicate_event`; an altered body and a wrong key → 401 `channel_signature_invalid`; ten minutes old → 401 `channel_signature_expired`.

## FIXED-880 — The web client did not load over plain http to a LAN address

**Severity: High. Area: Interface / start-up. Status: Fixed 2026-10-11 — found by the Web UI workflow.**

**Observed.** After FIXED-875 numbered every stop and steer, the tab named
itself with `crypto.randomUUID()` as `api.ts` loaded. Browsers offer
`randomUUID` only in a secure context — https, or `localhost` — so opening
Raiker at `http://192.168.x.x:8765` threw before anything was drawn and the
page stayed blank. The mocked end-to-end suite, served from
`http://raiker.test`, failed sixteen tests at the sign-in screen for the same
reason; the live round, on `127.0.0.1`, could not see it.

**Fixed.** The tab's name is eight bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues`, which
every context has, in the same `web-` and sixteen hex digits form.

**Evidence.** `controlSequence.test.ts` loads the client with no `randomUUID`
and fails without the fix; the mocked end-to-end suite passes.

## FIXED-881 — Two threat models described the GitHub credential and connector as they were before the vault and before writes

**Severity: Low. Area: Documentation / threat models. Status: Fixed 2026-10-12 — found reviewing the code for the DEC-21b amendment.**

Connector* and said comment and modify actions were "deliberately **not

approval-required) has shipped since B11. `docs/threat-models/git-push.md`
named `RAIKER_GITHUB_TOKEN` as the only push credential, though RAIKER-2022 had
moved it into the vault and lent it under grants. The permissions guide said a
push needs `RAIKER_GITHUB_TOKEN` set, contradicting the Build guide.

**Fixed.** The connector page describes reads and the two approval-gated
writes, states that it still uses the environment token and not the broker, and
points to the planned shared broker (ADD-27 GH-56); its index row is renamed.
The push page describes the vault credential, the grant, the legacy variable and
the three defects found with it (BUG-334, BUG-335, BUG-336). The permissions
guide and both known-limits pages say what a push needs today.

**Evidence.** Code read on 2026-10-12: `raiker/models/tool_registry.py`
(`github_write`), `raiker/runtime/executors/connectors.py`,
`raiker/runtime/git_credential.py`, `raiker/runtime/executors/tier1_git.py`;
the documentation link check passes.

## FIXED-882 — A push proposal ignored the token stored in Settings (was BUG-334)

**Severity: High. Area: Build / Git push. Status: Fixed 2026-10-12.**

**Observed.** The proposal step read only `RAIKER_GITHUB_TOKEN`; with the token
in the vault and nothing in the environment every proposed push was refused as
`push_credential_unset` before an approval was raised.

**Fixed.** The tool broker and the dashboard's preview ask the broker whether a
credential is configured (`token_configured()`), never for its value, and a
refusal names Settings → GitHub. The value is lent only at execution, under a
grant.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_git_push_path.py` — a vault-only token proposes and
pushes; no test in the file sets the environment variable any more.

## FIXED-883 — A "this session" Git grant was not tied to any session (was BUG-335)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / Git credential. Status: Fixed 2026-10-12.**

**Observed.** Settings granted with no session and the push asked with none, so
*this session* covered every chat and routine for an hour.

**Fixed.** A session grant needs a session (`git_grant_session_required`);
Settings offers only *once*; the push executor asks with the approval's
`origin_session_id`, and a grant for another conversation refuses
`git_grant_other_session`. Grants are also narrowed to operation, repository,
branch, credential and account (GH-17).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_git_credential_grant.py` through the executor, not the
store; `web/src/lib/views/settings/GitCredential.test.ts`.

## FIXED-884 — A push sent the branch as it was when it ran, not the commits that were approved (was BUG-336)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / Git push. Status: Fixed 2026-10-12.**

**Observed.** The approval showed a head and its commits; the push sent whatever
`refs/heads/<branch>` held at execution.

**Fixed.** Raising a push approval records the remote, its resolved URL, the
branch and the head SHA (`git_push_bindings`, RAIKER-2106). The push sends
`<approved-sha>:refs/heads/<branch>` and refuses `push_target_changed` naming
what moved; an approval with no binding refuses `push_binding_missing`. The
approval card shows the bound commit and warns when the branch has moved. The
pushed ref is read back into a receipt (GH-54).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_git_push_binding.py` (10);
`tests/test_git_push_path.py` read-back cases.

## FIXED-885 — An agent's push looked for a credential of its own, not the owner's

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / Git push / GitHub connector. Status: Fixed
2026-10-12 — found building ADD-27 GH-50.**

**Observed.** The push and fetch executors built the credential broker for the
acting principal. Under a standing decision that principal is the turn's agent,
which holds no credential, so an agent-run push or private fetch was refused as
`push_credential_unset` even with the owner's token stored; the API connector
had the same shape once it moved onto the broker.

**Fixed.** `credential_owner()` resolves an agent to the owner it acts for —
through the owner's account, or, on a machine with no password account, the one
human principal for the same user — and the executors, the connector and the
router's delegation check all use it.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_repository_delegations.py` (the connector reads with
the owner's vault credential as the turn's agent; the router finds the owner's
delegation for the agent).

## FIXED-886 — A standing grant or allow mode alone let an agent push or write to GitHub

**Severity: High. Area: Governance / Git and GitHub writes. Status: Fixed
2026-10-12 (ADD-27 GH-50, GH-52).**

**Observed.** A standing grant for `git_push`, or the push or GitHub capability
in *always allow* / *auto*, let an agent's push or pull request run with no
per-step approval and nothing naming the repository or branch.

**Fixed.** A push or GitHub write by an agent runs unprompted only under a
**repository delegation** the owner made: one repository, named operations
(merge, branch deletion, workflows and settings are never delegable), a branch
pattern that cannot reach the default branch, an expiry and an optional budget.
Before each step it is re-validated — delegation, credential, account,
installation, repository id — and spent; otherwise the step asks, and
`repository_delegation_refused` says why. The composer's *auto* / *skip* modes
send such a step to the approval queue instead of failing it. A child's
delegation is narrowed from its parent's and never wider.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_repository_delegations.py` (38): a read delegation
never writes, a PR delegation never merges, a branch delegation never reaches
another branch, a revocation mid-task parks the next step, an approved push
needs no delegation.

**Severity: Low. Area: Settings → GitHub. Status: Fixed 2026-10-12 — found
building the GitHub routes.**

without a repository, which an installation token is never minted without, so
it always failed `github_installation_needs_scope`; and an installation GitHub
stopped listing stayed *active*.

**Fixed.** Checking an installation asks GitHub for the App's installations;
one no longer listed is marked removed, and a GitHub that cannot be asked is an
error, not a pass.

**Evidence.** The `POST /api/github/credentials/{credential_id}/check` and
installation cases in `tests/test_api_contract_responses.py`.

## FIXED-888 — A Telegram turn's answer never went back over Telegram (was BUG-315)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Messaging / Telegram. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-315). DEC-14 steps 7–8. Owner decision 2026-10-13: a reply to the owner's own message is sent without asking, unless it carries sensitive information.**

**Observed.** A Telegram message on a *New turn* or *Side question* route ran a governed turn and the answer went back in the HTTP response to Telegram's webhook call, which Telegram ignores. The owner read every answer only in Raiker.

**Fixed.** When the owner's own Telegram message finishes its turn, the inbound route hands the answer to `RuntimeControlService.deliver_channel_reply`, which sends it through the governed `external_channel_runtime` executor as the owner — so the capability gate, a paused channel, the egress allowlist and the 4,096-character limit all still decide. An answer that the redaction pass would mask (keys, tokens, private keys, email addresses) or that the memory policy classes as credential- or secret-like is **held** instead: an outbound receipt with `held_at`, `reason_code = reply_held_sensitive`, the turn it carries and the message it answers, never the text. *Deliveries to review* offers **Read it**, **Send to chat** (`POST /api/channels/deliveries/{receipt_id}/send`, which re-reads the text from the conversation and sends it under the same receipt) and **Discard** (the existing *reviewed* mark). A held reply is not settled *outcome unknown* at start and is not trimmed with old receipts. The route now says *Sent back to your chat when you message Raiker*; another sender's message and a turn still waiting on an approval send nothing. Migration RAIKER-2110 adds `held_at`, `turn_id` and `reply_to_receipt_id`; events `channel_reply_delivered`, `channel_reply_failed`, `channel_reply_held`.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_channel_telegram_reply.py` (7), a contract case for the send route, `MessagingView.test.ts`, `channelSetup.test.ts`. Live: a real Anthropic turn answered the owner's Telegram update and the send left through the governed path — Telegram refused the round's placeholder bot token, which the receipt names — and an answer carrying an email address was held with Send to chat and Discard ([05](../screenshots/2026-10-13-ledger-round/05-messaging-held-and-failed-replies.png), [06](../screenshots/2026-10-13-ledger-round/06-route-says-replies-go-back.png), [07](../screenshots/2026-10-13-ledger-round/07-messaging-review-390-dark.png)). A real bot's delivered message is not proved: this host has no Telegram account.

## FIXED-889 — An instruction in the prompt stopped recall finding the memory it asked about (was BUG-313)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / recall. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-313). Owner decision 2026-10-13: a bounded fallback admits a memory holding two thirds of the question's content words.**

**Observed.** *What is my favourite tea? Answer in one sentence.* recalled nothing: the full-text match is an AND over every content word, so *answer* and *sentence* had to be in the memory.

**Fixed.** Words about the shape of the answer (*answer*, *reply*, *respond*, *sentence(s)*, *briefly*, *concisely*, *paragraph(s)*, *bullet(s)*) join the stopwords the strict match ignores. When the strict match still finds nothing, `search_approved_memory` asks the index again with the words OR-ed, reads a bounded candidate set in the index's own ranking, and admits a record only when it holds at least two thirds of the content words and never fewer than two; such a row carries `recall_match = "partial"`. Every eligibility condition — owner, scope, expiry, validity, supersession, sensitivity — is the same query's.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_retrieval_hardening.py` (3 new): the tea sentence and *Reply briefly* recall it; two of three words do, two of four and an unrelated overlap do not; another scope or owner never does. Live: a real Haiku 5.5 turn asked the original sentence, was given the memory and answered *Your favourite tea is Assam with a splash of oat milk.* ([03](../screenshots/2026-10-13-ledger-round/03-recall-despite-the-instruction.png)).

## FIXED-890 — Build's "Working in" named a project whose folder Build does not work in (was BUG-316)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / Projects. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-316). Owner decision 2026-10-13: the recommended relabel — no change to filesystem authority or command cwd.**

**Observed.** The composer said **Working in *project*** and the boundary inspector named the project first, while every relative read, write and command resolves against the workspace root.

**Fixed.** The server's boundary view (`GET /api/build/boundary`) carries `works_in`, the folder relative paths resolve against. The composer reads **Filed in *project* · works in *workspace***, and the inspector lists *Filed in* then *Works in — reads, writes and commands start here* before repository, environment and model.

## FIXED-891 — A stopped OpenAI-compatible stream recorded no usage (was BUG-333)

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / usage. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-333). DEC-24 step 2: "separate estimated from settled usage; account for cancelled calls that a provider still bills".**

**Observed.** OpenAI, OpenRouter and Ollama report usage only in a stream's last chunk, so a turn the owner stopped was recorded as nothing and every spending limit read it as free.

**Fixed.** A stopped stream with no provider count records an estimate — the request at four characters a token and the text already shown — in a ledger row marked `estimated` (migration RAIKER-2109). It counts in every total and limit, because the provider billed it; Models → Usage says *Includes N stopped requests estimated by Raiker*. A provider's own count is never marked.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_stopped_stream_usage.py` (3), `ProviderUsagePanel.test.ts` (2). Not exercised live: the round's provider was Anthropic, which reports input usage as the stream opens.

**Observed.** A run parked on an approval was continued on a new orchestrator whose meter started at zero, so a run that paused could spend its limit again after each approval.

**Fixed.** The suspension row keeps the run's metered spend (`spent_before_pause`: total and unpriced models); the resumed turn's meter starts from it. A malformed snapshot seeds nothing rather than failing the resume.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_turn_resume_after_approval.py` (2): $0.40 of a $0.50 limit survives the pause and the next $0.40 response stops the run.

## FIXED-893 — Deleting a project or a picture was not journalled, so a restore brought it back (was BUG-324)

**Severity: Low. Area: Storage / restore. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-324). DEC-24 step 5: deletion tombstones applied after a restore.**

**Observed.** Only forgotten and purged memories, deleted conversations and Git authority were journalled; a project deleted, a picture removed for good or a managed file removed after a backup came back with a restore.

**Fixed.** Three more kinds go in `.raiker/deletions.jsonl` — `project_delete` (with the conversations and tasks filed in it), `image_purge` and `managed_file_retire` — written by the store method that performs the deletion, content-free, and replayed into a restore with journaling off. Undoing a half-created project is not an owner's deletion and is not journalled. A task has no owner-facing delete of its own; it goes with its project or conversation, both journalled.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_lock_screen_recovery.py` (2): a project and a purged picture deleted after the backup stay deleted in the restored copy, and the journal holds no prompt text.

## FIXED-894 — Setup called an identity-linked Anthropic key connected and offered models it could not list (was BUG-332)

## FIXED-898 — A standing *Git writes* decision covered local branches and commits without a delegation (was BUG-337)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / Git writes. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-337). DEC-21b-J: delegated autonomy is repository- and branch-bound.**

**Observed.** Since GH-50 a push and a GitHub write ran unprompted only under a covering delegation; creating a branch and committing still followed the decision mode and standing grants alone.

**Fixed.** `GitWriteExecutor.repository_target` names the GitHub repository (the branch's upstream remote, else `origin`, else the only remote) and the branch — the one named for a branch, the checked-out one for a commit — so the router applies the delegation rule to both. A repository with no GitHub remote keeps the decision mode, since there is nothing to delegate.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_repository_delegations.py` (3) against a real repository: allow mode alone no longer branches for an agent, a `raiker/*` delegation covers `raiker/feature` and not `hotfix`.

## FIXED-899 — A delegation's repository identity was checked against the last discovery, not asked of GitHub (was BUG-338)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / delegations. Status: Fixed 2026-10-13 (was BUG-338). DEC-21b-G: identity re-checked before consequential operations.**

**Observed.** The router re-validated a delegation against Raiker's own records only, so a repository transferred or re-created since the last refresh was not seen until the next.

**Fixed.** Before a delegated push or pull request the router asks GitHub (`GET /repos/{owner}/{name}`) with the delegation's credential; a clean answer is reused for 60 seconds per delegation so a burst of steps asks once, while the local checks run on every step. A different id is `repository_identity_changed`, a 403/404 `repository_access_removed`, and GitHub out of reach `github_unreachable` — each parks the step for the owner.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_repository_delegations.py` (2): one question for two pushes, the third refused when the id changed; an unreachable GitHub blocks the step.

## FIXED-904 — Raiker had no window of its own: it opened as a browser tab

**Severity: High. Area: Desktop / application shell. Status: Fixed 2026-10-17 — DESK-01, DESK-02, DESK-05, DESK-11. Owner decision: the desktop window is the default experience.**

**Observed.** `raiker-app` started the host and handed the owner a browser tab. The desktop design kept a native window deferred, so Raiker had no menu, no shortcuts, no window of its own, and a stray tab was the application.

**Fixed.** `desktop/` is an Electron shell (the reference personal agent desktop app's shape: a window over the agent's own core). It attaches to a running host (`--raiker-url`) or starts the bundled one, and exposes one frozen bridge, `window.raikerDesktop`, with three operations. `raiker/app/desktop_shell.py` finds the window — `RAIKER_DESKTOP_SHELL`, the packaged shell around a frozen host, or `desktop/` in a source checkout — and `raiker-app` opens it by default. `--browser` opens the browser instead; a missing window falls back to the browser *and says why*. The decision and its reasons are recorded in [the desktop design](../architecture/DESKTOP_DISTRIBUTION_DESIGN.md#desktop-window-desk-01desk-14).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_desktop_shell.py` (discovery on three platforms, fallback wording, `--browser`); `desktop/e2e/shell.spec.ts` (bridge shape, frozen, no `require`/`process` in the page); a plain `raiker-app` from a source checkout opened the window on a real X display (`desk-11-raiker-app-window.png`, 2026-10-17 round).

## FIXED-905 — A desktop shell had no way to learn where the host it started was listening

**Severity: Medium. Area: Desktop / host lifecycle. Status: Fixed 2026-10-17 — DESK-03.**

**Observed.** `raiker-app` chose its port at run time and announced it only on stdout, and it opened the browser after a fixed 1.2-second timer whether or not the server had bound.

**Fixed.** `raiker-app --ready-file PATH` writes `{url, port, joined, pid}` atomically once `/api/health` answers — or at once when it joins a running host. A file rather than stdout: the shell discards the host's output so closing the window can never break the host's pipe. The window or browser now opens when the host answers, not after a guess.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_desktop_shell.py::test_the_ready_file_is_written_whole`, `…joining_a_running_host_writes_the_ready_file…`, `…readiness_waits_for_the_host…`; `desktop/test/host.test.ts`.

## FIXED-906 — A desktop window could have become a second, ungoverned browser

**Severity: High. Area: Desktop / security. Status: Fixed 2026-10-17 — DESK-04. Preventive: the guards shipped with the window.**

**Observed.** Any Electron window that loads a URL can be navigated, open popups, request device permissions and, misconfigured, reach Node.

**Fixed.** The page runs with context isolation, the Chromium sandbox and no Node integration; webviews are refused. Navigation is pinned to the one loopback Raiker origin the window was opened for (`desktop/src/origin.ts`): web links go to the owner's browser, another local Raiker instance gets its own window, and `file:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, custom schemes and credentialled URLs are refused. Only notifications, clipboard writes and audio-only media may be granted, and only to that origin. A non-loopback `--raiker-url` is refused by name.

**Evidence.** `desktop/test/origin.test.ts`; `desktop/e2e/shell.spec.ts` (navigation, permissions, refused address, unreachable host).

## FIXED-907 — The web app had no window chrome for a desktop window

**Severity: Medium. Area: Desktop / web UI. Status: Fixed 2026-10-17 — DESK-06. Found in the round: CSS `env(titlebar-area-*)` goes stale after a resize.**

**Observed.** A frameless window needs a draggable title bar and room for the platform's window buttons; a page built for a browser tab has neither.

**Fixed.** In the window `<html data-desktop-shell=…>` makes the top bar the title bar (pressable controls opt out of dragging), reserves room for macOS's traffic lights over the navigation and for Windows/Linux controls at the top bar's end, and colours those controls to the theme. Before sign-in a drag strip takes the top bar's place and the sign-in page starts below it. The controls' width is measured with the Window Controls Overlay API's `geometrychange`: the first round showed Chromium does not re-evaluate `env(titlebar-area-*)` for an existing element on resize, which left 290 px reserved for 113 px of controls.

**Evidence.** `web/src/lib/desktopShell.test.ts`; `desktop-live.spec.ts` asserts the drag regions and a non-zero controls width in a narrow window; screenshots `desktop-03-home.png`, `desktop-07-dark.png`, `desktop-08-narrow.png`, and the emulated macOS captures `mac-02-home.png`, `mac-03-narrow.png`.

## FIXED-920 — Signed installers did not carry the desktop window, and needed a system Python (was BUG-343)

**Severity: High (raised as Low). Area: Desktop / release. Status: Fixed 2026-10-17 (was BUG-343) — [ADR-0003](../adr/ADR-0003-desktop-distribution.md), DIST-01 – DIST-12.**

**Observed.** `release.yml` built and signed the browser-launch payload and wrapped it in `.pkg`/`.msi`/`.deb`/AppImage installers whose post-install step ran `python3 -m venv`, so no published installer could install on a machine without Python 3.11. Nothing built, signed or tested the Electron package, and the window had been exercised on Linux only. The audit for this fix also found the release never built the governed-command runner, and that a frozen host could not start its update helper.

**Fixed.** The release product is the desktop package: `scripts/build_desktop_app.py` freezes the host (with the command runner and the in-app guide), writes `installation.json`, smoke-tests the frozen host, and packages it with the pinned electron-builder as NSIS + MSI (Windows), dmg + zip (macOS Apple silicon and Intel), and AppImage + deb + rpm (Linux x86-64 and ARM64). `.github/workflows/desktop-package.yml` builds, installs, smoke-tests, opens the installed window, completes onboarding and uninstalls on each platform's own runner; `release.yml` calls it with the signing identities and publishes `desktop-<channel>.json`. First run gained This device, Permissions and Check stages; the vault key moved to the OS key store; desktop updates verify a signed manifest before installing.

**Evidence.** [Release acceptance matrix](RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md): every native target PASS in CI run 39041854653 (commit `914b60a`), including the real Windows and macOS windows this item asked for. Signing with real identities is unexercised until the release owner adds them; the pipeline refuses to publish without them.

## FIXED-921 — A cloud Ollama model was described as never leaving the device (was BUG-340)

**Severity: High. Area: Models / setup / privacy truthfulness. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 (was BUG-340).**

**Observed.** First-run setup recommended a running Ollama with *"its models never leave this device"*, and kept saying so after the owner chose `gpt-oss:20b-cloud`, a model Ollama serves from ollama.com. The comparison table placed the same model *On this device*, and Models' own `-cloud` check missed `…:cloud` names.

**Root cause.** The claim was made about the runtime (Ollama runs here), never about the model. Ollama's `/api/tags` already says where each model runs (`remote_host` on cloud models), and nothing read it.

**Fixed.** `raiker/models/local_service.py` records each served model's location (`device`, or the host Ollama names; a Cloud-named model with no `remote_host` is treated as remote) and `ModelProfileView.model_locations` carries it. One rule, `web/src/lib/inferenceLocation.ts`, decides the wording everywhere: setup's recommendation earns the device claim only when every served model runs here and otherwise names ollama.com; the chosen model's line says where its requests go; the privacy step names the chosen model's destination; the comparison and Models' *Cloud inference* chip use the same rule.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_local_model_service.py`, `inferenceLocation.test.ts`, `firstRun.test.ts`, `modelComparison.test.ts`. Live: `web/e2e/bug-340-ollama-cloud-location-live.spec.ts` on a reset workspace against the real Ollama 0.40.5 on this host — no screen claims the device for the cloud model, and the turn was answered `RAIKER_E2E_OK` by `gpt-oss:20b-cloud` with the runtime's *model request completed* receipt (`docs/screenshots/2026-10-17-bug-340-ollama-cloud/01`–`06`). The *Local only* choice beside it is still unenforced — raised as [BUG-345](#fixed-947--local-only-was-a-setup-answer-nothing-enforced-was-bug-345).

## FIXED-922 — raiker-app joined a host serving a different workspace (was BUG-342)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Desktop / host lifecycle. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 (was BUG-342).**

**Observed.** With workspace A's host on 8765, `raiker-app --workspace B` opened A's sign-in page and never started B.

**Root cause.** `choose_port` asked `/api/health` whether *a* Raiker answered, never whose. A second defect hid under it on Windows: `port_is_free` probed with `SO_REUSEADDR`, which there lets a bind succeed over a live listener that set it too.

**Fixed.** `choose_port(preferred, workspace=…)` joins this workspace's own host wherever its `HostControl` record says it is, and otherwise passes over any Raiker on the preferred port like any other listener. `raiker-web` now writes and clears the same host record `raiker-app` does, so a web-started host is still joined rather than doubled. Windows probes with `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_app_launcher.py` (two workspaces and one preferred port over real sockets; a workspace's host joined on the port it recorded). Live: with `raiker-web` serving A on 8765, `raiker-app --workspace A` joined 8765 and `raiker-app --workspace B` started on 8766 with its own host record.

## FIXED-923 — Owner bootstrap emitted a password-form diagnostic (was BUG-341)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Account bootstrap / accessibility. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 (was BUG-341).**

**Observed.** A fresh workspace logged *"[DOM] Password forms should have (optionally hidden) username fields"* in Chromium, though the settled form was correct.

**Root cause.** Isolated in headed Chromium (the headless shell runs no password-form audit, which is why earlier isolated reproductions were silent): the sign-in form is drawn before bootstrap status answers, then grows a second password field in place when it does. The same final form drawn at once raises nothing; a form replaced whole raises nothing.

**Fixed.** `LoginView.svelte` draws the credentials form under `{#key registerIntent}`, so the switch from sign-in to registration replaces the form whole. The keyboard path, password visibility and the disabled-while-verifying state are unchanged. The lock screen's `<main>` also gained the `id="main"` its skip link targets.

**Evidence.** `LoginView.test.ts` (19). Headed Chromium on three fresh workspaces: no `[DOM]` diagnostic (three of three reproduced before). axe on the first-run form: 0 violations (was `region`, `skip-link`). Capture: `docs/screenshots/2026-10-17-bug-341-bootstrap/01-first-run-form-no-password-diagnostic.png`.

## FIXED-924 — A lapsed lease met an immutable receipt on Windows, and a redirect test saw a reset (was BUG-330)

**Severity: Low. Area: Tests / Windows / background execution. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 (BUG-330 remainder; the fixture half was [FIXED-901](#fixed-901--three-tests-assumed-linux-newlines-and-separators-part-of-bug-330)).**

**Observed.** On Windows the lease-reclaim test failed ten of ten (`command_receipt_immutable`) and the redirect test two of ten (`mcp_remote_unreachable`).

**Root cause.** `reconcile_leases` killed the process before writing the lease-expired receipt; the run's own watcher saw the exit and finalised first (termination is synchronous on Windows), so the honest receipt could not be written — product behaviour, not a test artefact. The redirect stand-in answered 307 without reading the POST body, and Windows resets a socket closed with unread data.

**Fixed.** `raiker/execution/commands/service.py` writes the receipt first and terminates after; the watcher then finds a terminal run and stands down. The stand-in reads the body as a real server does.

The full Windows run for this round found two more POSIX assumptions, both failing on clean `main` too: an exec-bit assertion on a Linux-only AppImage (`tests/test_desktop_update.py`, now asserted off Windows only) and an unquoted `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF` command whose backslashes `sh` ate (`tests/test_local_git_environment.py`, now quoted with forward slashes).

**Evidence.** Windows 11: `tests/test_background_execution.py` six of six; the lease test with `tests/test_mcp_remote_transport_trust.py` twelve of twelve; `tests/test_desktop_update.py` and `tests/test_local_git_environment.py` pass.
