## FIXED-927 — A Ready Ollama model without tool support failed every turn with HTTP 400

**Severity: High. Area: Models / Ollama / turns. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found in the BUG-318 round.**

**Observed.** `gemma3:1b`, chosen in setup and shown Ready, answered every Chat turn with *"the provider refused the request … provider_http_error:http_400"*.

**Root cause.** Raiker sends the turn's tool list to every Ollama model. Ollama refuses tools for a model it lists without the `tools` capability (`does not support tools`), and the readiness check — a catalogue read — never sends tools, so it said Ready.

**Fixed.** The liveness probe records each model's published `capabilities`; `ModelRouter` sends a turn on a model the service lists without `tools` with no tools at all. That is only ever less authority: the model answers and can call nothing. A model whose capabilities were not published is not second-guessed.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_router.py`, `tests/test_local_model_service.py`; the FIXED-925 round answered on `gemma3:1b`.

**Severity: Low. Area: Settings. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found in the BUG-280 round.**

**Observed.** Re-selecting the stored time zone showed *You have unsaved changes* beside *All changes saved* and an unsaved dot on General, and the leave guard then held the owner on a page with nothing to save.

**Root cause.** `SettingsView.save()` set `dirty = true` for any change event, whatever the value.

**Fixed.** It recomputes dirty state from the keys that differ from the server snapshot.

**Evidence.** `SettingsView.test.ts` ("does not call choosing the stored value an unsaved change"); reproduced and re-checked in the browser.

## FIXED-930 — An Anthropic workspace the key cannot use was reported as a missing model

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / Anthropic identity-linked keys. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18.**

**Observed.** Checked against the live API with the round's identity-linked key: a well-formed workspace id the key has no access to answers HTTP **404** *Workspace `…` not found.* Raiker read only 400s as workspace refusals, so this became `model_not_found` and sent the owner looking for a model.

**Fixed.** `workspace_id_rejected` also reads a 404 whose body says a workspace was not found, so it reaches the owner as `provider_workspace_invalid` with *Check the workspace ID*. Anthropic's authentication guide sends every key type as `Authorization: Bearer` and calls `x-api-key` legacy; Raiker now sends Anthropic keys the same way, with `anthropic-workspace-id` only when one is named.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_provider_workspace_named.py`. Live, through Raiker's own provider: the identity-linked key with its workspace listed `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-fable-5-1` and answered a one-token request *OK*; without the workspace the API refused with the missing-workspace message Raiker already classifies; with a wrong workspace it now reports `provider_workspace_invalid:http_404`.

## FIXED-931 — OpenRouter declining one model for Raiker was reported as a rejected credential

**Severity: High. Area: Models / OpenRouter / readiness. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reported by the owner.**

**Observed.** With a valid OpenRouter key, the readiness check on `thinkingmachines/inkling:free` said *OpenRouter rejected the saved credential during execution*. The same key answered `openai/gpt-4o-mini` and `openrouter/free`.

**Root cause.** OpenRouter answers that model with HTTP 403 *"… is only available on agentic harnesses"* (`failed_routing_step: "Gate Free Endpoints by Agentic Harness"`): it offers some free models only to apps on its own list. Raiker read every 403 as an authentication failure. Checked live: with honest Raiker attribution the model is still refused; it answers for an app on OpenRouter's list. Raiker does not present itself as another app.

**Fixed.** `ProviderModelRefusedError` (a kind of "cannot execute this model") is raised for a 403 whose body names a routing gate or an "only available" restriction. Readiness says *OpenRouter accepted the key but will not run {model} for Raiker — choose another model*; a turn says the key is fine; the Models next step is **Choose another model**. OpenRouter requests now carry `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title: Raiker`.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_provider_model_refused.py`. Live through Raiker's provider with the owner's key: `inkling:free` → `provider_model_refused:http_403` with the new sentence; `openrouter/free` → *OK*.

## FIXED-934 — OpenRouter requests could not be kept away from providers that store prompts

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / OpenRouter / privacy. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reference personal agent parity (`provider_routing`).**

**Observed.** OpenRouter routes one model to whichever of several providers it chooses, some of which retain prompts. reference personal agent lets the owner say `data_collection: deny` and what to prefer; Raiker sent nothing, so the owner had no say.

**Fixed.** `PUT /api/models/{profile_id}/routing` (OpenRouter only, needs a saved connection) stores `data_collection` (`deny` or account default) and `sort` (price, throughput, latency or default) beside the connection without touching the key; re-pasting the key keeps them. The factory sends them as OpenRouter's `provider` object on every request through that connection, and only OpenRouter's own values ever reach a request. The connected OpenRouter card shows **OpenRouter routing** with both choices. Nothing is denied by default: live, `deny` once left `openrouter/free` with no provider (429), so it is the owner's choice and the card says so.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_openrouter_routing.py` (9), `ModelsView.test.ts` (routing control), contract case for the route. Live through Raiker's provider with the owner's key: `openai/gpt-4o-mini` and `openrouter/free` answered with and without `deny`; with `deny` OpenRouter served `openrouter/free` from Phala instead of Nvidia.

## FIXED-936 — A tool-less model behind a custom endpoint failed every turn

**Severity: High. Area: Models / turns / custom endpoints. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18.**

**Observed.** Through a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `gemma3:1b` answered every turn *the provider refused the request … provider_http_error:http_400*. FIXED-927 sends no tools to such a model only for the built-in Ollama profile, whose catalogue says so; a custom endpoint publishes nothing.

**Fixed.** A 400 whose body says the endpoint refuses tools (Ollama, vLLM without auto tool choice, llama.cpp without `--jinja`) is `tool_calls_unsupported`; the router asks again once without tools (streamed or not, only before anything streamed) and remembers the model for the process, so later turns skip the refused attempt. Only ever less authority.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_router.py` ("an endpoint that refuses tools is asked again without them"). Live: the FIXED-935 turn answered after the retry.

## FIXED-937 — One rate-limited or spent key ended the turn

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / credentials / resilience. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reference personal agent parity (credential pools).**

**Fixed.** A connection may hold up to three backup keys (`api_key_2`…`api_key_4`), entered under **Advanced** in the connect dialog; backups alone join a saved connection, re-pasting the main key keeps them, `[]` clears them. `raiker/models/credential_pool.py` orders the keys for each request — rested first, benched last — and the router moves a request refused with a rate limit or an empty quota to the next key in the same turn (streamed or not, only before anything streamed), benching the refused key for 60 s or 1 h. Authentication failures are never rotated past. The card shows how many backups are saved and, while a key rests, which key is in use and why. Keys are named only by position; no view, event or sentence carries a value.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_credential_pool.py` (9). A real 429 or empty balance cannot be produced on demand from this host, so the rotation is proven against fake providers raising the classified errors the transport produces.

## FIXED-938 — Side work had to use the turn's own model

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / side tasks. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reference personal agent parity (`auxiliary.<task>`).**

**Fixed.** `raiker/models/side_tasks.py` keeps, per owner, an ordered chain of up to three models for **summarise** and **vision** (`PUT /api/model-side-tasks`, gate-manager only; the models view returns `side_tasks`). Compaction tries the summarising chain and then the turn's own model, recording which model wrote the summary. When the turn's model cannot see an attached image, the vision chain describes it and the description joins the prompt as text, marked as a description and as untrusted content, with `attachment_image_described` naming the model (`attachment_image_description_failed` per failure); with no chain the image is withheld as before. A vision chain refuses a model that does not accept images. **Runtime & routing → Side-task models** edits both.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_side_task_models.py` (6), `SideTaskModels.test.ts` (2). Live: `gemma3:1b` (no vision) was asked what an attached image says; the vision chain (`gemma4:31b-cloud` through Ollama) described it and `gemma3:1b` answered *BLUE 42*, the text drawn in the image (`docs/screenshots/2026-10-18-provider-evidence/08`–`09`).

## FIXED-939 — A model chosen on a second custom endpoint would run on the first

**Severity: High. Area: Models / custom endpoints / routing. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found building FIXED-938, a defect in FIXED-935.**

**Root cause.** A turn names its model as `(provider, model)`. All four OpenAI-compatible slots share the provider and ship `<model>`, so a lookup by provider alone landed on the first slot — its endpoint and key — whenever no slot-specific copy happened to be registered first (two slots serving the same model name, or any path that resolves without registering).

**Fixed.** `ModelProfileRegistry.turn_token` names a profile by its id when its provider is shared by several placeholder profiles, and `resolve` accepts a profile id in the provider position; the gateway and the owner runtime use it.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_named_custom_endpoints.py` ("a turn names a shared slot by profile id and reaches that slot"); gateway, orchestrator, registry, selection and fallback suites pass.

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / Ollama / vision. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found building FIXED-938.**

**Root cause.** The Ollama profile cannot declare vision for every model it may serve, so the provider dropped every image, including for models Ollama lists with `vision` (`gemma4:31b-cloud`), and the turn reported them withheld.

## FIXED-941 — Nothing said whether a self-hosted server could call tools

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / local servers. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reference personal agent parity (local-server requirements).**

**Fixed.** `POST /api/models/{profile_id}/server-check` (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, MLX and OpenAI-compatible profiles only) sends one request with one harmless tool through the same governed provider path a turn uses, with native tool-call parsing only so a text reply is never mistaken for a call, and classifies it native, as text, refused, not called or unavailable. It reads the serving context from a loopback server's own status endpoint (Ollama `/api/ps`, llama.cpp `/props`, LM Studio `/api/v0/models`, vLLM `/v1/models`), never from an off-machine host, and names the setting that fixes each finding. **Details → Check this server** shows it.

## FIXED-944 — All four providers answer the owner identity question with the chosen name

**Severity: Low. Area: Live evidence / providers. Status: Closed 2026-10-18 — was BUG-290.**

**Observed before the fix.** The original provider round could reach only
Anthropic. OpenAI and OpenRouter were stopped by the host's egress environment,
and Ollama was not installed, so the identity contract was real-provider evidence
for only one of the four requested routes.

**Verified.** The owner entered each hosted-provider key through Raiker's Models
UI. Anthropic Haiku 4.5, OpenAI GPT-4o Mini and OpenRouter GPT-4o Mini each
answered the same owner-name question with **Rahul S**, not an internal
`principal_user_…` identifier. The existing live Ollama scenario asked the same
question through `gpt-oss:20b-cloud` and also received the chosen name. Browser
captures for all four answers were reviewed; the Ollama capture remains at
`docs/screenshots/2026-09-13-release-readiness/identity-answered-by-name-ollama.png`.

**Harness evidence.** `owner-identity-live.spec.ts` keeps the real-turn contract,
including the assertion that the response contains the chosen name and excludes
the internal principal identifier. Its chosen-name setup scenario passed live in
this round after FIXED-946.

## FIXED-945 — Design offered image models from unconnected providers

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / Models. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found testing BUG-287.**

**Observed.** With OpenAI connected and Gemini unconnected, Design's image-model
picker offered both providers. Choosing the unconnected profile could only lead
to a missing-credential refusal, despite the page already having enough model
readiness state to avoid presenting it.

**Fixed.** Design now applies the shared `isReachableProfile` rule before it
builds the image-model choices. The picker therefore contains image-capable
profiles only when their local runtime or hosted connection is reachable.

**Evidence.** `DesignView.test.ts` first reproduced the extra Gemini choice, then
passed with only connected OpenAI offered (**22/22** focused tests). A rebuilt
live page was inspected and its picker offered only OpenAI. The production web
build also completed.

## FIXED-947 — *Local only* was a setup answer nothing enforced (was BUG-345)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Setup / privacy. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — was
BUG-345.**

**Observed.** First-run setup offered *Local only — Model requests stay on this
device.* The answer was stored as `privacy_mode = "local_first"` and nothing
read it: a turn on a cloud Ollama model, or on a hosted provider connected
later, was sent exactly as under *Local, and the providers I connect*.

**Decision.** BUG-345 offered enforcing the answer as a routing rule, rewording
it as a preference, or removing it. The owner chose **removal** on 2026-10-18.
Keeping requests on the device remains possible the way it always actually
worked: by choosing a model that runs here, whose destination the step already
names (FIXED-921 / BUG-340).

**Fixed.**

* The Privacy stage is now a statement, *Where your model requests go*, with
  **Back** and **Continue**. Continue records the acknowledgement as before.
* `SetupUpdateRequest.privacy_mode` and `SetupState.privacy_mode` accept only
  `balanced`; a request carrying `local_first` is refused with 422.
* Migration `RAIKER-2111-setup-privacy-local-only-removed` rewrites any stored
  `local_first` row to `balanced` — the behaviour it always had — so no stored
  answer keeps a promise the runtime never made.
* The API contract, the getting-started guide and every live spec that drove
  the old buttons (web first launch, BUG-340, the 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-04
  rounds, the shared `hosted-provider` setup walker, both desktop specs) follow.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_setup_state.py` adds a refusal test and a migration
rewrite test (**7/7** with the restart-persistence file). Web unit tests for
`firstRun`, `ModelSetupView` and `App` pass (**55**, one existing skip); the new
view test clicks **Continue** and reads `privacy_mode: "balanced"` from the PUT.
`first-launch-live.spec.ts` passed **1/1** against a fresh `raiker-web`
workspace, and its `first-run-03-privacy.png` capture was reviewed: heading,
statement, Back and Continue, consistent with the other stages.

## FIXED-948 — The first-launch live spec skipped the Check stage by reading it too early

**Severity: Low. Area: Live test harness. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — found
verifying FIXED-947.**

**Observed.** After the Privacy stage, `first-launch-live.spec.ts` asked
`isVisible({ timeout: 5_000 })` whether *Checking your installation* was shown.
`isVisible` returns at once and ignores its timeout, so the read raced the save,
returned false, and the spec then waited thirty seconds for *Setup saved* while
the page sat on the Check stage.

**Fixed.** The spec waits for the title to leave the Privacy stage, then, on the
Check stage, waits for its **Continue** to be enabled before pressing it.

**Evidence.** The first run against a fresh workspace failed exactly as above;
after the edit the spec passed **1/1** against a new fresh workspace.

## FIXED-949 — A Windows-only crash dump had no CI job that could catch it again (was BUG-312)

**Severity: Low. Area: Tests / Windows / CI. Status: Closed 2026-10-18 — was
BUG-312.**

**Observed.** One of 28 local Windows runs of
`tests/test_instance_runtime_lifecycle.py` with
`tests/test_windows_internal_paths.py` ended in a fault-handler dump cut off
before its first frame. 37 later local runs, 15 of them under
`-X faulthandler`, were clean. Every Python CI job ran on Linux, so a
recurrence could only ever be seen by hand.

**Closure condition.** BUG-312 stayed open "until a complete dump names a frame
or the suite has a Windows job that would catch it". The second half is now
true.

**Fixed.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains **Windows lifecycle tests**: on
`windows-latest` it installs the package and runs the pair three times under
`python -X faulthandler`, so a recurrence fails the push with a complete dump in
the log instead of disappearing.

**Evidence.** The job passed on its first run, CI run 39163161663 on commit
`43ec4908`. Locally the pair passed again under `-X faulthandler` (21 tests),
and the full local suite passed on Windows. If the job ever prints a dump, the
frame it names is a new defect.

## FIXED-950 — The issue-to-pull-request routine can now be scheduled as a Build task (BUG-339, reduced)

**Severity: Low. Area: Tasks / GitHub. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — reduces
BUG-339; its RR-40 live evidence stays open there.**

**Observed.** `raiker/github/routines.py` could say which steps of the
issue-to-PR routine would run under a delegation, and nothing could carry them
out: scheduled routines run read-only subagents.

**Approach.** reference personal agent's and reference gateway's scheduled jobs run a full agent turn
from a stored prompt. Raiker's scheduled **Tasks** already do, and the authority
router already runs an AI-proposed repository write unprompted only under a
covering, re-validated delegation, parking anything else for approval. So no
second runner was built: the template now becomes a Build task.

**Fixed.**

* `issue_to_pr_task_draft` turns a plan into the task's title and instructions:
  the steps with their decisions, the work branch, the issue as untrusted data,
  the never-list, stop-and-report on a refusal, receipts at the end.
* `POST /api/github/routines/issue-to-pr` is read-only and person-only. It
  returns the plan and the draft, re-validating the delegation against GitHub
  (BUG-338), and starts nothing.
* Settings → GitHub → *Issue to pull request* shows the plan with a decision per
  step and schedules it as a Build task in a chosen project through the
  existing `POST /api/tasks`, with its idempotency key, model check and
  schedule terms. The Build guide documents it.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_api_github.py` adds a route test: GitHub unreachable
makes the preview *blocked*; with a covering delegation every write *runs under
the delegation*; with none every write *asks*; the preview creates no task and
spends no delegation action (**50/50** with `test_repository_delegations.py`).
`GitHubConnection.test.ts` drives preview → project → schedule and reads the
POST body (**7/7**). The new `bug-339-issue-to-pr-routine-live.spec.ts` passed
**1/1** against a fresh `raiker-web`, and its `routine-plan.png` capture was
reviewed: each write step reads *Asks you first*, the never-list names merge,
and **Schedule as a Build task** stays disabled until a project is chosen.

## FIXED-952 — A Build change read as done whether or not anything checked it (BR-D01, first slice)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / verification. Status: Fixed 2026-10-18 — the
first slice of [BR-D01](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); the rest stays on its row.**

**Observed.** A Build turn that changed files ended on the model's prose. A
plausible patch, or *I ran the tests and they pass*, was indistinguishable from a
change something had actually checked, which BR-09 forbids.

**Approach.** Independence comes from two halves the model controls neither of:
the **commands are the owner's**, declared on the project, and the **results are
the runtime's**, read from `tool_actions` and `command_runs`. No new execution
path: the agent runs the checks through the ordinary governed command tools, so
every policy, grant and approval still applies.

**Fixed.**

* `project_contexts.checks_json` (migration `RAIKER-2112-project-checks`); checks
  save with the project context under its revision guard, at most ten of 300
  characters, de-duplicated; the nearest folder that declares checks decides.
* The project context a Build turn receives lists the checks and asks for each
  to run exactly as written after the last change.
* `raiker/control/build_outcome.py` classifies a turn as `no_change`,
  `completed_verified`, `completed_unverified`, `failed`, `blocked` or
  `outcome_unknown`, with one row per check: passed, failed, not run, ran before
  the last change, waiting for approval, or did not finish.
* `GET /api/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}/outcome`, read-only and owner-scoped.
* **Projects → Overview → Checks** edits them; Build shows the outcome under
  each settled turn, in the page's ok/warn/danger tokens, and nothing for a turn
  that changed nothing. The Build guide documents both.
* Contract cases for this route and for the BUG-339 issue-to-PR route, whose
  missing case had turned `main`'s CI red.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_outcome.py` (classifier: no change, no checks,
all passed, hidden failing test, check before the last change, lookalike
command, timeout, waiting approval, failed write; API: save, keep on an older
editor, refuse eleven, gatherer text, outcome read, 404) and
`tests/test_projects.py` pass (**40**); contract responses **401/401**.
`BuildOutcome.test.ts` and the new `ProjectsView` case pass; full web suite
**2272** passed. `br-d01-build-outcome-live.spec.ts` passed **1/1** against a
fresh `raiker-web`, and `01-project-checks.png` was reviewed. Driving a real model
turn that changes a file found [BUG-346](#fixed-953--an-accepted-build-write-wrote-nothing-and-its-row-read-failed-bug-346); in that run the
outcome read the turn as `no_change`, correctly claiming nothing.

## FIXED-953 — An accepted Build write wrote nothing and its row read failed (BUG-346)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / approvals. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — closes
BUG-346, found 2026-10-18 driving [BR-D01](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md) live.**

**Observed.** On a fresh workspace with **File writes** and **Patch apply** on,
Ollama `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` kept through the Models picker, a Build turn proposed
`write_file notes.txt`. After **Accept** the turn resumed, the row read **Write
file notes.txt failed**, the model called its call invalid or said the
capability still needed approval, no file was written, and the proposal's
`tool_actions` row stayed `approval_required`.

**Root cause.** Not the model and not the arguments: a stub model proposing a
fixed call, and the real `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` driven in-process, both wrote the
file when the account was the CLI bootstrap owner. The difference was the
account. On an account created through first run, an unset gate is read
fail-closed, and the relay that turns an accepted decision into the effect
(`approval_execution_relay`) has its own gate that nothing turned on —
Permissions' **Set up for Build** preset listed file writes, patch apply, git
writes and checkpoint restore, and not the relay. Accept therefore took the
metadata-only path, which governance requires, while: the card said only that
Raiker re-governs before running; the model was told *Raiker records approvals
for this capability without performing them*; the live row mapped that to
**failed**; and no code ever moved the proposal's own `tool_actions` row off
`approval_required`, so BR-D01 read the turn as `no_change`.

**Fixed.** Governance is unchanged — the relay's gate still decides, and its
unset reading is still off.

* **Set up for Build** now turns on **Approval execution relay** first ("Apply a
  change once you accept it"), so the owner's one deliberate Build decision makes
  Accept mean apply. It is still a per-capability, audited transition; no
  decision mode changes.
* `ApprovalExecutionBridge.metadata_only_gate` names the switch (the relay, or
  the target capability) that keeps an otherwise-executable approval from
  running. The approval detail notice says so before the decision (*Accepting
  this records your decision only — it will not be carried out, because
  **Approval execution relay** is off in Permissions*), and Build shows it on the
  card in *Waiting on you*.
* The resolve response carries `not_executed_reason: metadata_only:<gate>`; Build
  says *Accepted, but nothing was applied — … is off in Permissions* instead of
  *Decision recorded*.
* The resumed turn's tool result carries the same reason code and a note naming
  the switch, so the model tells the owner what to turn on rather than calling
  its call invalid or proposing it again.
* `SQLiteStore` settles the proposing call's `tool_actions` row when its approval
  reaches a terminal state: executed → `success`, execution failed → `failed`,
  denied → `denied`, approved-without-running or expired → `failed`, guarded on
  `approval_required` so a settled row is never overwritten. BR-D01 now counts an
  accepted write as a change.

**After-turn readiness.** The *No readiness check exists for this exact model*
message did not recur: in the fresh-workspace run below the model was kept
through the picker without **Check**, the gateway's first-use check admitted the
turn, and after it the composer showed no readiness warning and **Run** enabled
as soon as text was typed. The spec asserts both.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_bug_346_accepted_build_write.py` (account created
through `/api/auth/register`, scripted model, real routes): with the Build gates
and the relay on, Accept writes `notes.txt` once, the resumed turn completes on
a `success` outcome, the row is `success` and the outcome route reads
`completed_unverified`; with only File writes and Patch apply on, the card names
the relay, Accept writes nothing, the response and the model's outcome name
`metadata_only:approval_execution_relay`, and the row is `failed`; a rejection
settles the row `denied`. All four failed on `850d42d4` and pass now. The
approval, resume, relay, broker, capability and checkpoint suites pass, with two
older asserts updated from the generic sentence to the named gate. Ruff, mypy
(`raiker apps tests --platform linux`), svelte-check and the web unit suite pass
(`recentPages.test.ts` fails locally only, under Node 25's built-in
`localStorage`, untouched here). Live: `br-d01-build-outcome-live.spec.ts`
passed **2/2** against a `raiker-web` on a workspace reset with
`scripts/reset_live_workspace.py` — account created through first run,
`gpt-oss:120b-cloud` kept through the Ollama picker without **Check**, **Set up
for Build** pressed, a check declared on a new project, then a Build turn whose
accepted `write_file` wrote `notes.txt` (`hello from Build`, read back from
disk), its row read **Write file notes.txt done**, and the outcome read **Not
verified** with `python -m pytest -q` *not run after the last change*. Captures
`02-set-up-for-build.png`, `03-waiting-on-you.png` and
`04-accepted-write-not-verified.png` (under
`docs/screenshots/2026-10-18-br-d01-build-outcome/`, not committed) were
reviewed. No provider key was typed; the model was the existing Ollama Cloud
sign-in.

**Not changed here.** A managed project's Build turn still writes the path the
model names relative to the workspace root (`notes.txt` landed beside the
project folder, not inside it); the path authority for a managed project is the
workspace, as before.

## FIXED-954 — A Build check counted wherever it ran, and a written file was never read back (BR-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / verification. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
two BR-D01 faults [FIXED-952](#fixed-952--a-build-change-read-as-done-whether-or-not-anything-checked-it-br-d01-first-slice) left open; BR-D01 is now implemented on its
row in [`BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md`](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Observed.** A declared check counted wherever it ran. `run_command` always ran
at the workspace root, so for a repository in a sub-folder the check either
could not be run in the right place at all or, run at the root, checked a
different tree and still read **Verified**. Separately, nothing read a written
file back: a write the runtime recorded as successful, whose file was deleted
before the check, still read as verified.

**Root cause.** The run's working directory was stored only inside the
encrypted execution material, so the outcome could not read it; the command
tool offered no working directory; and the classifier read `tool_actions` and
`command_runs` but never the disk.

**Fixed.**

* `run_command` takes an optional `cwd`, resolved through the workspace read
  authority (symlinks resolved, nothing outside the workspace, must be a
  directory) — `command_cwd_outside_workspace` / `command_cwd_not_a_directory`
  otherwise. The grant, allowlist and placement checks are unchanged.
* `command_runs.cwd` (migration `RAIKER-2113-command-run-cwd`) stores the
  workspace-relative folder in plain form; it is on `CommandRunView` too.
* `classify_build_turn` takes the turn's repository folder: the same check run
  elsewhere reads `wrong_directory` and never `passed`. The project context asks
  for the checks to run with `cwd` set to the selected repository's folder.
* `read_back_writes` reads each written file back — `matches`, `present`,
  `changed_since`, `missing`, `unreadable` — through the same read authority. A
  `missing` destination keeps an otherwise passing turn **Not verified**; a later
  change does not undo verification.
* Build's outcome line says *ran outside the repository folder (in the workspace
  root)* and lists any file *no longer on disk* or *changed since this turn*.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_target_and_review.py` (repository folder
verifies, workspace root reads `wrong_directory`, folder spellings compare,
no recorded target accepts any folder, read-back states, read-back never leaves
the workspace, missing destination demotes, later change does not, `cwd`
confinement including a symlink escape, the run stores its folder, and the API
outcome with a real git repository) and `tests/test_build_outcome.py` pass;
`BuildOutcome.test.ts` adds the wrong-folder and read-back cases.

## FIXED-955 — A Build turn named a repository, not the target it ran against (BR-D02, first slice)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / execution target. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 —
the first slice of [BR-D02](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); concurrent worktrees stay
on its row.**

**Observed.** BR-02 requires a named, validated target before a write-capable
turn. Build showed a repository label. When the selected local folder had moved,
`resolve_repository_root` fell back to the workspace root, so a Build turn ran
its git and file tools against a tree the owner had not chosen, with only a
header warning.

**Fixed.**

* `raiker/control/build_target.py` describes the target from the runtime's own
  sources: folder, repository identity (GitHub coordinate, or the `origin`
  remote with credentials stripped), branch, commit, selected command
  environment and where code would be placed. A SHA-256 fingerprint covers
  identity, folder, branch and environment — not the commit (a turn's own commit
  is not drift) and not placement (a timed re-measurement must not invent
  drift).
* `GET /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/target`, read-only and owner-scoped.
* The gateway records the target for every Build turn
  (`build_turn_targets`, migration `RAIKER-2114-build-turn-targets`, first record
  wins) and **refuses a Build turn whose selected folder is gone** before it
  starts — streamed as `build_target_missing` — instead of running in the
  workspace root.
* The outcome compares the recorded target with the current one; drift (branch,
  folder, repository, environment, or a vanished folder) keeps a passing turn
  **Not verified**, and the line says what moved. Otherwise it says where the
  turn ran: *Ran in app on main from 6e99715*.
* The Build header shows the target chip — `main · 6e99715` and **Sandbox** /
  **This computer** / **Your environment** — with the folder, identity,
  environment and fingerprint as its tooltip and accessible name.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_target_and_review.py` (credential stripping, a
real repository described and fingerprinted, a commit is not drift and a branch
switch is, moved folder / coordinate / none, a vanished folder is drift,
record-once, the gateway refusal and binding, the route, and the outcome reading
a branch switched under the turn); `BuildTargetChip.test.ts` (3). Live:
`br-d02-d04-build-target-and-review-live.spec.ts` passed **4/4** against a fresh
`raiker-web` on a workspace reset with `scripts/reset_live_workspace.py`, with
Anthropic connected through Models using the round's identity-linked key and
workspace ID: the chip read `main · 6e99715 · This computer`; a real
`claude-haiku-4-5` Build turn wrote `app/NOTES.md` (read back from disk) and its
outcome read **Not verified** — no checks declared — *Ran in app on main from
6e99715*; and with the folder moved away the header said so and the turn
answered *The repository folder app is no longer in the workspace, so this Build
turn did not start* with no file written. Captures `01-build-target-chip.png`,
`02-real-turn-outcome-target.png` and `05-missing-target-refused.png` (under
`docs/screenshots/2026-10-19-br-d02-d04-build-target-review/`, not committed) were reviewed.

## FIXED-956 — A patch was shown, never reviewed, and every look was a new look (BR-D04, first slice)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the first
slice of [BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); independent validators and selected
model review stay on its row.**

**Observed.** Build's Changes pane showed the diff. Nothing repeatable said what
had been checked in it, and nothing could tell a finding already raised on this
patch from a new one.

**Fixed.**

* `raiker/review/patch_review.py` reviews one exact unified diff — the working
  tree's, built by the helpers a commit is built from — with precise,
  deterministic rules: possible credential (value never echoed), merge conflict
  marker, debugger breakpoint in a source file of that language, CI/workflow
  definition changed (left to the owner, BR-12), instruction-like text (BR-04),
  and source changed without a test. Each finding has severity, category,
  confidence, file and line, evidence and a next step.
* Reviews are stored by the SHA-256 of the patch (`patch_reviews`, migration
  `RAIKER-2115-patch-reviews`): the same patch returns the stored review with
  `reused: true`, any edit is a different review.
* `GET` / `POST /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/review`; the POST reviews and stores
  and changes no file.
* Changes shows **Review this patch** above the diff, then the findings in the
  page's danger/warn tokens, and **Reviewed** with the fingerprint for a stored
  review.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_target_and_review.py` (each seeded problem at its
line, no secret in the output, false-positive controls — a function named
`ignore_previous`, documentation mentioning `breakpoint()` and `=======`, a
variable named `debuggerEnabled` — stay quiet, same patch same findings, and the
routes storing exactly one review); `PatchReview.test.ts` (3). Live: on the
same round a seeded credential-shaped assignment and `breakpoint()` read
*Possible credential added* `src/service.py:2`, *Debugging statement left in*
`src/service.py:3` and *Source changed without a test change*, with no part of
the value on the page; after a reload the same patch read **Reviewed ·
e5d8a713** and offered no second review. Captures `03-patch-review-findings.png`
and `04-patch-review-stored.png` were reviewed.

## FIXED-957 — Nothing proved an injected fault could not read as verified (BR-D06, first slice)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / testing. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the first
slice of [BR-D06](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); restart and provider faults injected
into a running host stay on its row.**

**Fixed.** `tests/test_build_fault_boundaries.py` asserts a verified baseline,
then injects thirteen faults one at a time — a failed write, a change after the
checks, a check lost on restart, cancelled, timed out or still running, a
provider that died before the checks, a hidden failing test, a check in the
wrong folder, a destination removed, a branch switched or a folder vanished
under the turn, and a check waiting for approval — and asserts each lands on its
truthful outcome and never `completed_verified` (**14/14**).

## FIXED-958 — A commit Raiker made could not say so, and nothing could check a claim that it did (BR-D05, first slice)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / provenance. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
first slice of [BR-D05](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); signed evidence stays on its
row.**

**Observed.** A commit Raiker recorded on the owner's approval was
indistinguishable in history from one the owner typed. A reviewer of the
repository had only the model's account of what produced a change.

**Fixed.**

* `raiker/control/build_provenance.py` builds `Raiker-Session` / `Raiker-Turn`
  trailers only from ids matching `sess_…` / `turn_…` (8–64 safe characters), so
  a path, a newline-smuggled second trailer, a token or model text is never
  written. `create_commit` appends them as the message's final paragraph;
  staging is unchanged.
* `GitWriteExecutor` names the proposing conversation — `origin_session_id` for
  an approval resolved from the inbox — and the turn only when the record says it
  belongs to that conversation.
* `GET /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/provenance` reads the last twenty commits'
  trailers back: `recorded` when this account holds that session and turn,
  `unrecorded` when they claim Raiker and nothing here backs them, `none`
  otherwise. Nothing reads a trailer to allow anything.
* **Changes → Recent commits** labels them **Made in Raiker** and **Says Raiker —
  no record here**.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py` (trailer shapes and
injection refusals, a real commit carrying both trailers and reading back
`recorded`, a hand-typed trailer reading `unrecorded`, the executor never pairing
a session with another conversation's turn, and the route);
`RecentCommits.test.ts` (2). Live: see [FIXED-959](#fixed-959--two-build-conversations-could-write-one-checkout-with-no-way-to-give-either-its-own-br-03).

## FIXED-959 — Two Build conversations could write one checkout, with no way to give either its own (BR-03)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / execution target. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 —
BR-03 in [BR-D02](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); Windows and cancel evidence stay on
its row.**

**Observed.** BR-03 requires concurrent write-capable work to use separate
worktrees and owned branches. Build had one checkout per repository, and two
conversations could run Build turns into it at the same time, each changing the
other's files and diff.

**Fixed.**

* `raiker/control/build_worktrees.py`: `create_worktree` adds
  `<repo>.worktrees/<name>` on a new `raiker/<name>` branch from HEAD, with
  repository hooks off; it refuses an invalid name, an existing branch
  (`branch_exists`), a branch checked out elsewhere (`branch_in_use`), an
  existing folder, a repository with no commits, a folder that is not a
  repository root, and a repository that is the workspace itself (its sibling
  would be outside the workspace). `remove_worktree` removes only a clean linked
  worktree, refuses uncommitted work (`worktree_has_uncommitted_changes`) and
  the main checkout (`not_a_task_worktree`), and keeps the branch.
* `POST /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/worktrees` connects the worktree as its own
  repository (without moving the selection); `DELETE
  /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/worktree` removes and forgets it. Both are audited
  as repository connect/disconnect events.
* The gateway refuses a Build turn while another conversation's Build turn is
  running against the same folder, streamed as `build_target_busy`, and names a
  worktree as the way to run both. A turn quiet for fifteen minutes is treated as
  abandoned so a dead host cannot hold a folder.
* The repository panel offers **New worktree** on a local repository and
  **Remove worktree** on a task worktree, with each refusal in words.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py` (create, separate
target fingerprint, main checkout unmoved, existing branch, invalid name,
uncommitted work refused and kept, removal keeps the branch and its commit,
main checkout not removable, workspace-root repository refused, a second
conversation refused, the same conversation and a finished turn not blocking,
an abandoned turn not holding the folder); `RepoConnector.test.ts` (2 new).
Live: `br-d02-d05-worktree-provenance-live.spec.ts` against a fresh
`raiker-web` with Anthropic connected through Models: **New worktree** made
`svc.worktrees/notes` on `raiker/notes`, the header read `raiker/notes · <head>`
while `svc` stayed on `main`; a real `claude-haiku-4-5` Build turn wrote
`NOTES.md` and committed it with `git_commit` after two **Accept**s — the commit
carried `Raiker-Session` and `Raiker-Turn`, `svc`'s own HEAD did not move, and
**Recent commits** read **Made in Raiker** for it and nothing for `init`;
**Remove worktree** with an untracked file in it was refused and the file stayed,
and once clean the worktree went and `raiker/notes` still held the commit.
Captures under `docs/screenshots/2026-10-19-br-d02-d05-worktree-provenance/` (not committed) were reviewed. Reviewing them found the removal refusal printed under the connect form at the foot of the panel, far from the button that raised it; worktree refusals now render beside the repository list, re-checked live on a second worktree (`raiker/second`: refused while dirty, removed once clean, branch kept).

## FIXED-960 — A parked Build turn resumed wherever the repository had moved to (BR-07)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / recovery. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
target half of BR-07; delegation and credential revalidation at resume stay on
[BR-D02](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md)'s row.**

**Observed.** A Build turn parked on an approval resumed under whatever the
repository was by then. If the owner switched branch or moved the folder while
the card waited, the continuation carried on its plan in a place it had never
inspected.

**Fixed.** Before a parked turn is claimed, the gateway compares its recorded
target with the current one. On drift it claims the parked turn, finalizes it as
`target_changed`, closes the turn as failed with the moved fields named, and
refuses with `build_target_changed` (409). Build says *This turn was not
continued: the folder, repository, branch or environment it started on has
changed since. Start a new turn here.* and does not retry.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py` (no drift is a
no-op; a branch switched under a parked turn raises `build_target_changed`,
leaves the suspended row `target_changed` and the turn `failed`);
`approvalResume.test.ts` classifies the code.

## FIXED-961 — A turn read as verified while its own patch review held a high-severity finding (BR-D04)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — part of
[BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Fixed.** The outcome reads the stored review of the patch in the turn's
repository now — it never runs one — and a high-severity finding on it keeps a
passing turn **Not verified** with the reason named; the outcome line says *The
review of the current patch has 1 high-severity finding — see Changes.*

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py` (clean and
medium-only reviews still verify, a high finding does not; the outcome route
reads `review: null` before a review and the high count after one);
`BuildOutcome.test.ts`.

## FIXED-962 — Restart and provider faults were proven only against the classifier's inputs (BR-D06)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / testing. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the second
slice of [BR-D06](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Fixed.** Two faults are now injected through the real stores and routes rather
than into the classifier's inputs: a background check left `running` with no
exit code — what a host that went away mid-check leaves in `command_runs` —
reads `outcome_unknown` through the outcome route
(`tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py`); and a provider that fails on
the continuation after an accepted write, through the real prompt, resolve and
resume routes with a scripted provider, leaves the written file on disk and the
turn **Not verified** (`tests/test_build_fault_provider.py`).

## FIXED-963 — A stopped, partly applied or waiting Build turn read as one of the other outcomes (BR-09)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / verification. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 —
completes BR-09's named outcomes on [BR-D01](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Observed.** BR-09 names `partially_completed` and `stopped` beside the
outcomes Build already reported, and neither existed. A turn the owner stopped
after a write read **Not verified** or even **Verified**; one where two of three
writes were refused read as a whole change; and a turn whose only write was still
waiting for approval read `no_change` and showed nothing.

**Fixed.** `classify_build_turn` takes the turn's own recorded status and the
statuses of every proposed write: a stopped turn that changed files reads
`stopped` (a failed check still reads `failed`); writes that partly applied read
`partially_completed` with `unapplied_writes`; a write still waiting reads
`blocked` with `pending_writes` — *A change this turn proposed is waiting for
your approval; nothing has changed yet*. Build labels them **Stopped**, **Partly
applied** and **Waiting on you**, and says how many proposed changes did not
apply.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_review_lifecycle.py` (stopped, stopped-but-failed,
stopped-with-no-change, partial, waiting) and `BuildOutcome.test.ts`.

## FIXED-964 — The patch review checked patterns, never whether the code still parsed (BR-D04)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
independent-validator half of [BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md); selected model
review stays on its row.**

**Observed.** The exact-patch review matched patterns in added lines. A change
that left a file unparseable passed it with *no findings*, and BR-D04 asks for
independent validators against the same patch.

**Fixed.** `parse_findings` parses each changed source or test file through the
governed `LanguageIntelligenceService` — the same service and gate the agent's
`diagnostics` tool and Build's file viewer use, so the three never disagree — and
each syntax error is a high-severity *File does not parse* finding at its line.
With **Language intelligence** off, the review carries an info finding *Changed
files were not parsed* instead of implying the files are fine. The validator
runs once per patch, inside the stored review.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_review_lifecycle.py` (a syntax error found at its
file with the gate on; *not run* with it off). Live: see
[FIXED-966](#fixed-966--a-finding-could-be-read-but-not-acted-on-without-retyping-it-br-d04-bounded-repair).

## FIXED-965 — Every review was a fresh list, with no word on what was new, fixed or stale (BR-D04)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — part of
[BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Fixed.** Each new review is compared with the repository's previous one: a
finding is `new` or `still_present`, matched by rule and file so a line that only
moved is not a new problem, and the previous review's findings that are gone are
listed as `resolved`. A read of a patch with no review yet returns the latest
earlier review as `previous`, so Changes says *The last review was of an earlier
version of this patch*. Changes marks **New** findings and lists **Fixed since
the last review**. Every review — taken or reused — appends a
`patch_review_completed` event with the fingerprint, counts, new and resolved
numbers only (catalogued in `EVENT_CATALOG.md`).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_review_lifecycle.py` (moved credential still
present, removed breakpoint resolved, conflict marker new; the stale read; two
audit events, neither carrying patch text); `PatchReview.test.ts`.

## FIXED-966 — A finding could be read but not acted on without retyping it (BR-D04 bounded repair)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — bounded repair
on [BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Fixed.** **Ask Raiker to fix** on a finding writes one scoped request into the
Build composer — the file and line, the finding and its next step, *Change only
what this finding needs, then run the project's checks. Do not commit, push or
merge.* — and focuses it. It calls nothing, so the repair is one more ordinary
turn the owner reads and sends, under the same modes and approvals, and the
review cannot loop on itself.

**Evidence.** `PatchReview.test.ts` (the request text, and no request made by the
click). Live: `br-d04-review-repair-live.spec.ts` against a fresh `raiker-web` with Anthropic connected through Models: a file broken so it no longer parses read *File does not parse* `calc.py:4` (*'(' was never closed.*); **Ask Raiker to fix** put *Fix this patch review finding in calc.py at line 4: File does not parse…* in the composer and sent nothing; sent, a real `claude-haiku-4-5` turn repaired the file after the owner's **Accept**; Changes then said the last review was of an earlier version, and reviewing again listed *File does not parse* under **Fixed since the last review**. Running it found [FIXED-968](#fixed-968--changes-kept-showing-the-tree-from-before-accept-applied-a-change) and a missing space in the resolved list, both fixed. Captures under `docs/screenshots/2026-10-19-br-d04-review-repair/` (not committed) were reviewed.

## FIXED-967 — Provenance, review and scheduled Build runs were invisible where the owner decides (BR-D03, BR-D05)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / tasks / provenance. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 —
the outcome foundation of [BR-D03](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md) and the disclosure
half of BR-D05.**

**Fixed.**

* A task's attempts now carry the session and turn they ran (`TaskAttemptView`),
  and a Build task's attempt history shows that turn's outcome — the same
  component and record a Build turn shows — so a scheduled issue-to-PR run reads
  **Verified**, **Not verified**, **Partly applied** or **Stopped** on its own
  history.
* The commit approval says, before the owner decides, that the commit message
  will end with `Raiker-Session` and `Raiker-Turn` lines.
* The Windows CI job now runs the Build target, worktree, provenance and outcome
  tests, so target binding has Windows evidence on every push; the directory
  symlink case, which needs a privilege the runner lacks, is Linux-only.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_review_lifecycle.py` (the approval body names the
trailers; an attempt names its turn); `TaskHistory.test.ts` (a Build attempt
shows the outcome, a Chat attempt asks for none). Live: on the same round, asked to commit, the Git commit card in Approvals read *The commit message will end with Raiker-Session and Raiker-Turn lines naming the conversation it came from.* above the diff, before **Approve and execute once** (`04-commit-approval-names-provenance.png`).

## FIXED-968 — Changes kept showing the tree from before Accept applied a change

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / workbench. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — found
driving [BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md) live.**

**Observed.** A Build turn proposed a write; the owner pressed **Accept**; the
continuation applied it. Changes still showed the diff from before — and so did
its patch review, which kept the broken file's findings although the file on
disk was fixed. Reloading the page showed the truth.

**Root cause.** The workbench re-read the working tree only when a *fresh* turn's
stream ended. An accepted change is applied by the continuation the approval
resumes, which ends in `resumeTurn`, and that path never bumped the re-read.

**Fixed.** `resumeTurn` now signals that the working tree may have changed when
the continuation settles, exactly as a fresh turn does, so Changes, its patch
review, the target chip and Recent commits re-read.

**Evidence.** The live round in [FIXED-966](#fixed-966--a-finding-could-be-read-but-not-acted-on-without-retyping-it-br-d04-bounded-repair) failed at *the
last review was of an earlier version* before the fix and passed after it.

## FIXED-969 — A patch was reviewed by rules, never by the model the owner chose (BR-D04)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — closes
[BR-D04](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md)'s "selected model review" remainder.**

**Observed.** The exact-patch review ran deterministic rules and a parse
validator. BR-10 also asks for selected model review against the same patch
fingerprint, and nothing let the owner ask a model to read the patch Build was
about to commit.

**Fixed.** `raiker/review/model_review.py` and
`POST /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/review/model`:

* the exact working-tree diff is credential-redacted and delimited as untrusted
  data, with no tools offered, and sent to the model chosen in the Build
  composer through the owner's own router (their gates, egress allowlist and
  connections);
* the answer is read strictly: findings outside the changed files are dropped,
  an unverified *high* is shown as medium at most, each is marked
  `source: model`, and an answer that is not the JSON asked for is refused as
  `model_review_unreadable` and stores nothing;
* the reading is stored by patch fingerprint **and** provider/model
  (`patch_model_reviews`), so the same model is never asked twice about one
  patch, and is audited as `patch_model_review_completed` — model, fingerprint
  and counts, never the patch or the answer;
* a model finding never decides `completed_verified`.

**Changes → Patch review → Model review** names the model (**Ask the Anthropic assistant Haiku
5.5 to review**), shows the findings with *These are its reading, not checks*,
and offers **Ask Raiker to fix** on each.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_model_review.py` (redaction and framing, strict
parsing, unreadable answers, once-per-patch-and-model with no second call,
content-free audit, a model finding not deciding verification);
`PatchReview.test.ts`; the API contract case. Live: see
[FIXED-978](#fixed-978--a-model-review-with-no-explicit-choice-went-to-a-placeholder-model-and-failed-with-a-bare-502).

## FIXED-970 — A stored review could be changed, and a signed commit said nothing (BR-D05)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / provenance. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — closes
[BR-D05](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Observed.** A stored review was a database row: anything that could write it
could drop a finding and the owner would read the edited list as the review.
And Recent commits said nothing about a commit the owner had signed.

**Fixed.** `raiker/review/review_attestation.py` signs every review when it is
taken — the deterministic one and each model reading — with this
installation's Ed25519 issuer key (the key that already signs per-turn machine
identities), over a digest of the review bound to owner, repository, patch
fingerprint and kind. Every read verifies it: `verified`, `invalid`,
`unknown_key` or `unsigned`. The owner is sent the state, key id and time,
never the signature bytes. Changes shows **Signed here**, or *This stored
review no longer matches the signature Raiker made when it was taken … don't
rely on these findings*. Recent commits reads Git's own `%G?` verdict on each
commit and shows **Signed**, **Signed — key not trusted here**, **Bad
signature** and the rest; an unsigned commit shows nothing. Raiker still never
signs a commit itself.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_model_review.py` (a taken review verifies; one
with a finding dropped reads `invalid`; a model reading is signed; an unsigned
one says so; an unsigned commit reads `none`); `PatchReview.test.ts` and
`RecentCommits.test.ts`. Live: `02-review-signed-here.png`.

## FIXED-971 — A parked Build turn resumed after its delegation or credential was withdrawn (BR-07)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / recovery. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
delegation and credential half of BR-07, after
[FIXED-960](#fixed-960--a-parked-build-turn-resumed-wherever-the-repository-had-moved-to-br-07)'s target half.**

**Observed.** A Build turn parked on an approval was checked for target drift
before it resumed, and for nothing else. An owner who revoked the repository
delegation the turn was working under — or removed the Git credential it would
push with — while the card waited still had the turn continue its plan.

**Fixed.** The turn's target record now carries `authority`: the active
delegations on its repository's GitHub identity and the selected Git
credential's id and state (identifiers only). Before a parked turn is claimed,
the gateway compares them: a delegation now revoked, expired, exhausted or gone,
or a credential removed, replaced or in another state, finalizes the parked
turn as `authority_changed`, closes the turn as failed with what was lost, and
refuses with `build_authority_changed`. Build says *This turn was not
continued: a repository delegation it started under was revoked or ran out, or
the Git credential it would use was removed or replaced. Check Settings →
GitHub, then start a new turn.*

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_provenance_and_worktrees.py` (revoked delegation;
replaced credential; a turn that started with neither never drifts; a target
recorded before this has nothing to compare); `approvalResume.test.ts`.

## FIXED-972 — Nothing proved a stopped Build turn kept its target and let go of the folder (BR-D02)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / execution target. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 —
the cancel scenario BR-D02 named as still open.**

**Fixed.** `tests/test_build_cancel_mid_turn.py` drives a Build turn through
the real routes with only the provider scripted, and presses Stop while the
model is answering: the turn ends `stopped` with the model asked once, its
fingerprinted target is still recorded, its outcome reads `no_change` with no
drift, `running_turns_on_folder` no longer counts it, and a second
conversation's Build turn in the same checkout is admitted. It runs on the
Windows CI job with the other target tests. No product change was needed.

## FIXED-973 — No live host had ever been killed mid-check (BR-D06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / testing. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — closes
[BR-D06](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Fixed.** `scripts/build_restart_fault.py` runs a real `raiker-web` process —
routes, gateway, broker, command service, leases, store — with only the model
scripted, so it needs no credential. A Build turn writes a file (accepted
through the approval routes) and starts the project's declared check in the
background under a session command grant; the host is killed with `SIGKILL`
while the check runs; a new host is started on the same workspace.

Two variants, both run by the `build-faults` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
on every pull request and push to `main`:

* **reattach** — only the host dies. The turn reads `outcome_unknown` (*A check
  you declared did not finish*) while the check runs; the new host takes the
  surviving run back over and records its real exit, and only then can the turn
  read verified.
* **lost** — the host and the check die together. The run settles with a
  failed receipt and the turn never reads verified.

**Evidence.** Both variants passed on this host (2026-10-19). Writing the
harness showed that a check outlives its host and is reattached — the honest
behaviour, now stated in the scenario rather than assumed away.

## FIXED-974 — A pull request Raiker opened was known only from the create response (BR-12)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / GitHub. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — part of
[BR-D03](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Observed.** BR-12: *push output alone does not prove a PR exists*. A pull
request Raiker opened was recorded from GitHub's create response and nothing
else, and nowhere in Build listed it.

**Fixed.** After GitHub accepts a pull request, `GithubConnectorService` reads
it back with the same credential (`GET /repos/{repo}/pulls/{number}`) and
`raiker/github/receipts.py` stores a receipt (`pull_request_receipts`):
repository, number, URL, head and base branch, head commit, state and
`confirmed` / `mismatch` / `unconfirmed`. A failed read-back never fails a pull
request that exists; it is recorded as unconfirmed with what the create
response said. The approval result says *opened and confirmed by GitHub* or
*GitHub did not confirm it on read-back*. `pull_request_receipt_recorded` is
audited without the body or token. **Changes → Pull requests**
(`GET /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/pull-requests`) lists them.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_git_write_path.py` (confirmed, mismatch, unconfirmed;
no token in the receipt; no test reaches the network); `PullRequestReceipts.test.ts`.
RR-40's live run against a consented repository remains open on BR-D03.

## FIXED-975 — The Build header never said what a turn could do without asking (BR-01)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / delegation. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** `GET /api/code/repos/{repo_id}/target` adds `authority`: the active
delegations on the target's GitHub identity (operations, branch pattern, pull
request allowance, expiry, actions left) and whether a Git credential is
selected. The target chip adds **Delegated: push, pull request on raiker/\***
or **Writes ask you**; its tooltip lists each delegation and says *Merging is
never delegated: it stays with you, on GitHub*.

**Evidence.** `BuildTargetChip.test.ts`. Live: `01-target-writes-ask-you.png`
on a repository whose `origin` is a GitHub URL and that has no delegation.

## FIXED-976 — A scheduled Build task ran in whatever repository Build was pointed at (BR-02)

**Severity: High. Area: Build / tasks. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — the
dedicated-workspace part of [BR-D03](BUILD_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md).**

**Observed.** A Build task's cycles ran against the repository selected in
Build *at the time the cycle fired*. An issue-to-PR task scheduled for one
repository would carry its change into another if the owner had since pointed
Build elsewhere — BR-02: *a missing, moved, stale or mismatched target fails
closed*.

**Fixed.** Creating a Build task records the repository Build is pointed at
(`build_task_targets`); the scheduler passes the task id with each cycle; the
gateway refuses a cycle whose current target is another repository, none, or
the same reference on a different remote or folder — *This scheduled Build task
was set up for widget (widget), and Build is now pointed at notes, so this run
did not start and nothing was changed* — which the task's attempt history shows.
Settings → GitHub → *Issue to pull request* says where the task will run before
it is scheduled.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_task_target.py` (recorded at creation; refused
on another repository and on none; a turn that is not a task's is not held);
`GitHubConnection.test.ts`. Runs on the Windows CI job.

## FIXED-977 — A repair was never reviewed again, and a persisting finding looked new each time (BR-11)

**Severity: Low. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** After the owner presses **Ask Raiker to fix**, the next time the
working tree settles with a new patch Changes reviews it once by itself and
says *Reviewed again after the repair*; a later settle without a new request
reviews nothing. Each finding carries `reviews_present` — how many reviews in a
row raised it — and Changes shows **In 3 reviews in a row**. No bound was
invented: the repair stays owner-sent, so the loop is the owner's to continue,
and the count shows when it is not converging.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_review_lifecycle.py` (count grows, resets after
resolution); `PatchReview.test.ts` (one rereview after a repair, none without one).

## FIXED-978 — A model review with no explicit choice went to a placeholder model and failed with a bare 502

**Severity: Medium. Area: Build / review. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — found
driving [FIXED-969](#fixed-969--a-patch-was-reviewed-by-rules-never-by-the-model-the-owner-chose-br-d04) live.**

**Observed.** On a fresh `raiker-web` with Anthropic connected through Models
and Build on its default model, **Ask the model to review** answered
`502 Bad Gateway` and the pane showed a generic error.

**Root cause.** With no per-work choice the composer sent no model, and the
server fell back to the owner's stored selection — on this workspace still the
catalogue placeholder `ollama/<model>` — which the router then failed to reach.

**Fixed.** Build sends the model the composer will actually use (this work's
choice, else the default it shows), and the server refuses a placeholder as
`model_review_model_required` (*Choose a model in the composer first*) without
calling any provider.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_build_model_review.py::test_a_placeholder_default_is_refused_as_no_model_chosen`.


## Design workspace — structured documents (2026-10-19)

## FIXED-979 — A design was one picture, never a document of layers (DW-01, DW-02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / composition. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Observed.** Design held generated pictures and a one-image viewer. There was
no document a layout could live in: no frames, no layer that stayed text, no
stable id an edit or an agent could name.

**Fixed.** A **design document** (`raiker/design/document.py`) is frames holding
an ordered, nested layer tree — text, rectangle, ellipse, image, group and stack
— where every node has a stable id, geometry, rotation, opacity, visibility,
lock and the actor that created it. Every change is a **typed operation**
(`add_node`, `update_node`, `remove_node`, `move_node`, `group_nodes`, `ungroup`,
`add_frame`, `update_frame`, `remove_frame`, `duplicate_frame`) applied all or
nothing and checked field by field: ids unique across the document, colours
`#rrggbb`, sizes, counts and depth bounded, and a locked layer only shown,
hidden, renamed or unlocked. Documents are owner-scoped rows
(`design_documents`, migration `RAIKER-2119-design-documents`), filed in a
project only when the owner chooses one, and put in Recently deleted rather than
removed. Routes: `/api/design/documents` (list, create, read, rename/file,
delete, restore).

**Evidence.** `tests/test_design_documents.py` (all-or-nothing operations naming the refused one, locked layers, owner scoping, filing refused for another owner's project).

## FIXED-980 — A change made against an old copy of a design would have overwritten newer work (DW-08)

**Severity: High. Area: Design / versions. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** Every write names the version it was made against
(`base_version`) and is stored as the next numbered version with its actor,
kind, summary, scope (the ids it touched), operations and a snapshot
(`design_document_versions`). A change against an older version is applied on
top when it touches nothing changed since (`rebased: true`), and refused as
`design_version_conflict:<ids>` when it meets later work. The page reloads the
design on a conflict and says why the change did not land.

**Evidence.** `test_a_stale_change_is_rebased_when_disjoint_and_refused_when_it_meets_later_work`; `DesignDocuments.test.ts` (conflict said in words, base version sent).

## FIXED-981 — Undo meant regenerating a picture, not stepping back through the design (DW-08)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / versions. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Undo**, **Redo** and **Go back to this** act on the structured
state and are themselves new versions: an undo writes the state before the last
change and remembers what it undid, so a redo restores it, through any number of
steps; going back to version N adds a version on top. Nothing in the history is
removed, and each acts only on the version the owner is looking at.

**Evidence.** `test_undo_and_redo_are_new_versions_on_the_structured_state`; live: `dw-design-documents-live.spec.ts` (v5 → undo v6 → redo v7, History names both).

## FIXED-982 — There were no frames, layouts or responsive variants to design into (DW-03)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / composition. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** A frame starts from a named target — square or story social post,
A4 document page, 16:9 presentation, mobile or desktop screen, or custom — with
a background and an 8px grid that can be shown. A **stack** places its children
along a row or column with gap, padding and alignment, recomputed by the server
after every change, so a stored document is always the one drawn; a **group**
is the box around its children and moves them with it. **Make variant** copies a
frame at another target size, scaled once, and records `variant_of` so the link
is shown without implying the two stay identical.

**Evidence.** `test_a_stack_places_its_children_and_a_group_moves_with_them`, `test_a_variant_is_scaled_once_and_linked_to_its_source`; live: mobile variant named *variant of Frame 1*.

## FIXED-983 — Nothing could be edited directly on a design (DW-02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / web. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Design → Documents** (`DesignDocuments.svelte`) has three regions:
frames and layers on the left, the canvas in the middle, and Inspect / Agent /
System / Check / Export / History on the right. The canvas is the document
drawn as SVG. A layer is selected on the canvas or in Layers (front-most first,
nested, with show/hide and lock and an *agent* badge on what the agent made);
the inspector edits position, size, rotation, opacity, text, font, colour, fill,
radius, stack spacing and image fit; arrange offers forward, backward, group,
ungroup, duplicate and remove. The canvas is one keyboard stop: arrows nudge 1px
(Shift 10px), Delete removes, Escape clears the selection, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z
undo and redo. Below 80rem the right rail moves under the canvas; on a phone the
canvas comes first. `#/design?view=documents` opens on it.

**Evidence.** `DesignDocuments.test.ts`, `designDocument.test.ts`; live screenshots `02-canvas-layers-inspector.png`, `11-phone-width.png` (no horizontal overflow at 390px).

## FIXED-984 — A picture used in a design could be deleted without a word (DW-05)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / assets. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** An image layer is a **link** to a picture in Images
(`asset_id`), never a copy. `GET /api/design/assets/{asset_id}/usage` names the
live designs that place it, and **Delete** in Images asks first when there are
any. A design whose picture is in Recently deleted keeps its layer, draws it as
a placeholder, and Check names it.

**Evidence.** `test_an_asset_used_by_a_design_says_so`; the *assets* check in `test_validation_is_honest_about_what_it_can_and_cannot_tell`.

## FIXED-985 — Image controls could not say which provider supported them, and there was no crop (DW-03, DW-04)

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / assets. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** `GET /api/images` now carries `operations` — what each provider's
governed path really does (`openai`: generate, edit, variations, size;
`gemini`: generate, edit, variations), from `IMAGE_OPERATIONS` beside the code
that sends the request. The count control is disabled for a provider without
variations, and masks, outpainting and upscaling stay absent because no provider
path exists. Crop (a box of fractions) and fit (cover, contain, stretch) are
**non-destructive** properties of an image layer, drawn by the canvas and every
export; the picture itself never changes.

**Evidence.** `test_an_export_is_pinned_to_its_version_and_hash_and_never_flattens_the_document` (a cropped placed picture in the PNG); `DesignView.test.ts`.

## FIXED-986 — A design had no brand to follow (DW-06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / systems. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** A **design system** (`design_systems`) holds named colours, font
families and spacing, usage rules, the variables a finished design must use and
a note on where it came from. Saving one again writes the next version; no
document using an earlier version changes. Layers refer to it through
`fill_var`, `color_var`, `font_var` and a frame's `background_var`, and keep the
literal value they are drawn with.

They are called **variables**, not tokens, for a measured reason: the response
redactor discards any field whose name contains `token`, so `fill_token` and a
system's `tokens` reached the page as `***REDACTED***` in the first test run.

**Evidence.** `test_a_system_is_versioned_and_applied_only_through_a_preview` (v2 leaves a v1 design alone; invalid values named).

## FIXED-987 — Changing a design's brand would have rewritten it unseen (DW-06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / systems. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** Choosing a system is two explicit steps. **Preview the change**
(`POST …/system/preview`) lists every layer whose drawn value would change, from
what to what, and every variable the system does not define, and writes nothing.
**Apply to this design** writes exactly that plan to this one document as one
version that undo reverses; a locked layer is reported and left alone.

**Evidence.** `test_a_system_is_versioned_and_applied_only_through_a_preview`; live `05-system-preview.png`.

## FIXED-988 — There was no design agent, only an image prompt (DW-07)

**Severity: High. Area: Design / agent. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Agent → Propose changes** sends one named frame (credential-
redacted, delimited as untrusted data) and the owner's brief to the chat model
they choose, through their own router, gates and egress allowlist, with no
tools. The answer must be a plan (summary, hierarchy, assumptions, assets,
validation) and typed operations. Each operation is dry-run in order against the
version the proposal was made from and kept as **valid** or **refused** with its
reason: outside the target frame, an operation an agent may not use (frames),
placing an image, removing more than three layers, a locked layer, an unknown
id. Unreadable answers are said (`design_proposal_unreadable`), never shown as
an empty proposal. Nothing is applied; `design_proposal_created` is audited
without the brief or any text.

**Evidence.** `test_an_agent_proposal_is_bounded_vetted_and_never_applied_by_itself`, `test_an_agent_may_not_remove_a_large_subtree`, `test_an_unreadable_answer_is_said`; live with Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`: two valid operations proposed, version unchanged until accepted (`06-agent-proposal.png`).

## FIXED-989 — Accepting an agent's work could not be partial and could overwrite the owner's (DW-08, DW-D05)

**Severity: High. Area: Design / agent. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** Each valid operation has a box; **Accept selected** applies only
those, as one version marked `actor: agent` with the proposal id, and new layers
carry `created_by: agent`. An operation that touches a layer changed after the
proposal was made is a conflict: nothing is applied, the page names the layers,
and **Apply the rest, keep my changes** applies only the others. A proposal is
decided once; `design_proposal_decided` is audited with counts.

**Evidence.** `test_a_stale_proposal_never_overwrites_later_owner_work`; live `07-agent-accepted.png` (*Agent proposal accepted — Accepted 2 of 2*).

## FIXED-990 — Nothing checked a design before it left Raiker (DW-10)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / validation. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Check** (`GET …/validation`, `design-validate/1`) runs nine
checks — placed pictures resolve, alternative text, text overflow measured with
the export renderer, WCAG AA contrast against a solid colour behind the text,
fonts the export can draw, layers outside their frame, variables that resolve,
required variables used, colours from the system — and states each as
**Passed**, **Failed**, **Not supported by the export** or **Cannot be known
from the design** (text over a photo, translucent text). Each finding names its
frame and layer and opens it. The outcome is *passed* only when every check
passed.

**Evidence.** `test_validation_is_honest_about_what_it_can_and_cannot_tell`; live `08-checks.png`.

## FIXED-991 — A design could not be exported, and an export would not have said what it was (DW-11)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / export. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Export** writes one frame as PNG or PDF (raster, at 0.5×–2×), SVG
(text stays text, shapes stay shapes, placed pictures embedded with crop and
fit) or JSON (the frame's structure). Each export records the version, frame,
format, settings (including which font drew a raster), the validation outcome
and the file's SHA-256 (`design_exports`), is downloaded through the owner's
session, and is audited as `design_exported`. The stored document is never
flattened.

**Evidence.** `test_an_export_is_pinned_to_its_version_and_hash_and_never_flattens_the_document` (pixels of a cropped picture, `%PDF`, `<text>`); live PNG and SVG with hashes, download named `raiker-design-frame-1-vN.png`.

## FIXED-992 — A finished design could not reach Build except as a screenshot (DW-11)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / Build. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Fixed.** **Hand to Build** writes the selected frame at the current version
— document and version, content hash, validation outcome, the stated target,
the system's variables and every layer's type, geometry, text, colours and
image ids — as a bounded Markdown document stored as the owner's attachment
(`design_handoffs`, audited as `design_handed_off`). Build's composer carries it
on the next visit like any attached document, labelled untrusted. It grants
nothing: every code change still goes through Build's modes and approvals.

**Evidence.** `test_a_build_handoff_is_bounded_context_that_writes_no_code` (credential redacted, no file written); `DesignDocuments.test.ts`; live `10-build-carries-handoff.png`.

## FIXED-993 — A Build handoff's file name reached the page as [REDACTED_SECRET]

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / Build. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-19).** After **Hand to Build** the page read
*Ready in Build's composer as `[REDACTED_SECRET].md`*.

**Root cause.** The name was a hyphenated slug of the title and version — one
unbroken run of URL-safe characters over forty long — which the response
