redactor's entropy fallback treats as a credential.

**Fixed.** The handoff is named in words with spaces, *Design handoff Launch
post v10.md*.

**Evidence.** `test_a_build_handoff_is_bounded_context_that_writes_no_code` asserts the exact name; live re-run passed.

## FIXED-994 — PNG and PDF exports drew a box for an em dash and for accented letters

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / export. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-19).** *Launch day — 21 October* exported as
*Launch day ☐ 21 October*: the font bundled with Pillow has no glyph for the em
dash, and none for é, ñ or € either.

**Fixed.** Raster exports use the first broad sans font the host has (DejaVu
Sans, Arial, Liberation Sans, Helvetica) and fall back to the bundled one; the
export records which. A character that font cannot draw is named by Check
(*no glyph for 中*) before export.

**Evidence.** `test_a_character_the_export_font_cannot_draw_is_named_before_export`; live PNG re-inspected (`pillow:DejaVuSans.ttf`).

## FIXED-995 — Text that overflowed its box was clipped on the canvas but drawn in full in exports

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / web. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-19).** A 48px headline in a 72px box showed one
line on the canvas while Check said it needed 115px and the PNG drew two.

**Fixed.** The canvas draws text past its box, as exports do, so what Check
calls overflow is visible where it is fixed.

**Evidence.** Live `07-agent-accepted.png` (both lines visible).

## FIXED-996 — A conflicting edit's explanation vanished in the reload it caused

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / web. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19.**

**Observed.** Found by the component test: a change refused as
`design_version_conflict` reloaded the design, and the reload cleared the notice
that said why.

**Fixed.** The reload after a conflict keeps the notice: *This design changed
since you loaded it…*.

**Evidence.** `DesignDocuments.test.ts` — *says a conflict in words and reloads instead of writing over later work*.

## FIXED-997 — The Design wire types broke the API contract on Python 3.11

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / API. Status: Fixed 2026-10-19 — found by CI.**

**Observed.** CI's Python 3.11 job failed one test of 7214,
`test_the_generated_contract_files_are_current`: pydantic refuses a
`typing.TypedDict` before Python 3.12 (`typed-dict-version`). The round had been
verified on Python 3.13, where the standard-library class is accepted.

**Fixed.** `raiker/api/wire/design.py` imports `TypedDict` from
`typing_extensions`, as every other wire module does.

**Evidence.** The test failed before and passed after under a local Python 3.11
environment; mypy, ruff and SAST clean there too.


## FIXED-998 — A layer could only be moved with the arrow keys (DW-02, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / canvas. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** [BUG-348](TO_BE_FIXED.md#bug-348--the-design-canvas-is-edited-by-keyboard-and-inspector-only-and-five-dw-requirements-are-still-partial)
recorded that the canvas was edited by keyboard and inspector only: a layer
could be clicked and nudged a pixel at a time, never dragged.

**Fixed.** A layer is dragged on the canvas. The drag is previewed locally and
sent when the pointer is released as one operation list against the version on
screen, so a whole gesture is one version — rebased or refused like any other —
with whole-pixel coordinates. A locked layer does not move; a group moves its
children with it. The click that ends a drag no longer clears the selection,
and a click without a pointer press (a screen reader, a test) still selects.

**Evidence.** `designManipulation.test.ts` (*moves every unlocked top-level
layer in one operation list*); live `dw-design-round-two-live.spec.ts` test 1 —
one version per drag, a locked rectangle dragged 100px writes nothing.

## FIXED-999 — There were no resize or rotate handles (DW-02, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / canvas. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** The selected, unlocked layer shows eight resize handles and a rotate
handle, drawn at a constant screen size and turned with the layer. Resizing
keeps the opposite edge, never inverts a box or shrinks it below 1px, works
along a rotated layer's own sides, and keeps proportions with Shift on a corner.
Rotating follows the pointer about the layer's centre; Shift snaps to 15°. A
group shows only the rotate handle, because its box is derived from its
children. Each drag is one `update_node` version.

**Evidence.** `designManipulation.test.ts` (*keeps the opposite edge…*, *resizes
a rotated layer along its own sides*, *turns a pointer into a rotation*); live
`02-resized-and-rotated.png` (wider, rotated 75° with Shift; deltas are whole
pixels since [FIXED-1001](#fixed-1001--a-drag-snapped-to-nothing-and-showed-no-guides-dw-02-bug-348)).

## FIXED-1000 — Only one layer could be selected, so nothing could be aligned or distributed (DW-02, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / canvas. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** Shift, Ctrl or Cmd adds or removes a layer from the selection, on
the canvas and in Layers. With more than one selected, the inspector shows
**N layers selected** with **Align left / Centre / Align right / Align top /
Middle / Align bottom**, **Distribute across / down** (three or more), **Group**
(when they share a parent) and **Remove**. Arrow keys move the whole
selection. With one layer selected, **Centre in frame** and **Middle of frame**
align it to the frame. Each is one version; locked layers stay where they are.

**Evidence.** `designManipulation.test.ts` (*align and distribute*);
`DesignDocuments.test.ts` (*selects several layers with Shift and aligns them as
one change*); live test 2, `03-three-selected-aligned.png`.

## FIXED-1001 — A drag snapped to nothing and showed no guides (DW-02, BUG-348)

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / canvas. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** While dragging, the moving box's edges and centre snap to the
frame's edges and centre and to other layers' edges and centres within six
screen pixels, and fall back to the grid when it is shown; each matched line is
drawn as a dashed guide. Alt places freely. Drag and resize deltas are whole
pixels — the first live drag stored `x = 176.58` because the canvas is scaled.

**Evidence.** `designManipulation.test.ts` (*snapping*); live test 1 drags a
rectangle near the centre and stores `x = 420`, (1080 − 240) / 2;
`01-drag-snaps-to-centre.png`.

## FIXED-1002 — The owner's own picture or logo could not be brought into Design (DW-04, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / assets. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** **Image → Import your own picture…** uploads a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF
through `POST /api/design/assets/import`, which applies the image upload
validator (allowlisted type, size cap, content sniff) and records an `import`
asset: provider `owner`, no model, the file name and its pixel size, filed with
the design's project. It is placed on the frame at once and appears under
Images as **Imported**, *Your file … No provider has seen it.* Sending it to a
provider later — an edit under Images — is a separate, governed request. This
is also the source-image path BUG-287 asked for. Audited as
`design_asset_imported` (ids, size and hash only).

**Evidence.** `test_the_owners_picture_is_an_import_asset_with_no_provider`
(a PNG declared as JPEG is refused); live test 3, `04-imported-picture-placed.png`,
`05-images-names-it-imported.png`.

## FIXED-1003 — Images did not show a picture imported under Documents until the page was reloaded

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / web. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-20).** After importing a picture under Documents,
switching to **Images** read *Nothing generated yet*. The history line of an
imported picture then read *· 64x32*, an empty model name.

**Root cause.** Design read the gallery once when it mounted; switching tabs
reused that read. The history line printed `model`, which an import does not
have.

**Fixed.** Switching to Images reads the gallery again, and an imported
picture's line reads *Imported · 64x32*.

**Evidence.** Live test 3 re-run passed.

## FIXED-1004 — A design system could only be typed in by hand (DW-06, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / systems. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** **Import from a tokens file** reads CSS custom properties or a JSON
tokens file — flat, nested, or W3C design-tokens `$value`/`$type` — on this
machine (`POST /api/design/systems/tokens`, which writes nothing). Colours
(`#rgb` to `#rrggbbaa`), font families and px/rem sizes fill the New design
system form; every token it could not place is listed with its reason (*refers
to another variable*, *not a colour, font or size*), and the source note names
the file and its SHA-256. **Or colours from a picture** reads the dominant
colours of any picture the owner has — a logo, a screenshot — with Pillow,
ignoring transparent pixels (`GET /api/design/assets/{id}/palette`). The form
gains **Spacing**. Nothing is saved until **Save system**.

**Evidence.** `test_tokens_from_css_and_json_are_placed_or_skipped_with_a_reason`,
`test_reading_tokens_writes_no_system`, `test_a_palette_ignores_transparent_pixels`;
live test 5, `08-tokens-imported.png` (four values read, one skipped, brand-1
`#ff6600` from the imported logo).

## FIXED-1005 — A skipped token's name reached the page as REDACTED

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / API. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-20).** The token report read *Skipped 1:
\*\*\*REDACTED\*\*\*: not a colour, font or size* for `--shadow-sm`.

**Root cause.** The skipped entry's field was called `token`, and the response
redactor blanks any field by that name — the same family as
[FIXED-993](#fixed-993--a-build-handoffs-file-name-reached-the-page-as-redacted_secret).

**Fixed.** The field is `name` (`DesignTokenSkip`).

**Evidence.** Live test 5 asserts *shadow-sm: not a colour, font or size*.

## FIXED-1006 — Nothing in a design could be reused (DW-06, DW-10, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / composition. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** **Make component** keeps a copy of the selected layer — a group, a
shape, an instance — in the document as a named component drawn from (0, 0)
(`define_component`). **Components → Place** puts an instance on the frame: a
group linked by `component_id` whose layers are ordinary, editable copies with
fresh ids (`place_component`). Editing an instance never changes its
component; the inspector says whether it still matches, and **Update from
component** replaces its layers as one version (`update_instance`). Removing a
component keeps every instance's layers; Check's new **Component instances
link to a component in this design** fails for the broken link
(`design-validate/2`). The Build handoff names components and instances. A
component lives in its document; sharing one through a design system remains
in BUG-348.

**Evidence.** `test_a_component_is_placed_as_linked_ordinary_layers_and_updated_only_on_request`,
`test_a_broken_component_link_is_a_failed_check_and_instances_keep_their_layers`;
`designManipulation.test.ts` (*says when an instance no longer matches*); live
test 4, `06-component-instance.png`.

## FIXED-1007 — A layer could not carry a note (DW-08, BUG-348)

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / composition. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** The inspector's **Notes** section adds, resolves, reopens and
deletes notes on the selected layer or on the frame (`add_note`,
`update_note`, `remove_note`). A note names its author and is a version like
any change, so undo brings back what a note said. Open notes are numbered pins
on the canvas (**Show pins**) and a *note* badge in Layers. They are never
drawn into an export; open notes on a handed-off frame go to Build under
*Open notes*, credential-redacted.

**Evidence.** `test_notes_are_versioned_changes_on_real_targets` (unknown target
refused, version scope is the note, undo restores, handoff carries it); live
test 4, `07-note-pinned.png`.

## FIXED-1008 — A PDF export was a picture of the frame (DW-11, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / export. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Fixed.** **PDF (vector, selectable text)** (`vector_pdf`) draws the frame with
PDF's own operators (`raiker/design/pdf.py`): rectangles with their radius and
ellipses as paths, opacity as a graphics state, rotation as a transform, text
as real text in the same font the raster export uses — embedded, wrapped where
the PNG wraps it — and placed pictures embedded after crop and fit. The page is
the frame at 0.75 pt per pixel, so an A4 frame is an A4 page. Text is
Windows-1252; a character outside it is written as `?` and counted in the
export's settings (`characters_replaced`). The download is named `.pdf`.

**Evidence.** `test_a_vector_pdf_keeps_text_as_text_and_counts_what_it_could_not_encode`
(pypdf reads *Café —* back, 596 × 842 pt); live test 5 downloads
`raiker-design-frame-1-vN.pdf` starting `%PDF-1.4`, `09-vector-pdf-export.png`.

## FIXED-1009 — A proposal whose host stopped mid-call left no record (DW-12, BUG-348)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / agent. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** A proposal row was written only after the model answered, so a
host that stopped during the call left nothing to say a request had been sent.

**Fixed.** The row is written as `requesting` before the model is asked,
stamped with the host run. It becomes `pending` with the vetted operations,
`failed` with the refusal code when the call ends without a usable answer, and
reads as `outcome_unknown` once a later host run finds it still requesting —
whether the provider answered is not known, nothing was applied, and it can
never be accepted or retried on its own. The Agent panel says so and offers
**Ask again with this brief**.

**Evidence.** `test_a_failed_call_is_recorded_and_an_interrupted_one_reads_as_outcome_unknown`;
`DesignDocuments.test.ts` (*says when a proposal's outcome is unknown*); live
test 6 kills the host (`kill -9`) while Anthropic Haiku 4.5 is being asked,
restarts it, reads *Outcome unknown* (`10-proposal-outcome-unknown.png`), then
asks again and accepts (`11-proposal-after-restart.png`).

## FIXED-1010 — After a restart the design agent said no chat model was connected

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / web. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live.**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-20).** Re-opening a design right after the host
restarted, the Agent panel read *No chat model is connected* although Anthropic
was; once models were read, the picker showed a blank choice.

**Root cause.** The model list was read once when Documents mounted, and the
picker was bound to an empty choice the first model only stood in for.

**Fixed.** Opening the Agent panel reads the models again, and the picker
always shows the model a proposal will use.

**Evidence.** Live test 6 re-run; `DesignDocuments.test.ts`.

## FIXED-1011 — A Design audit event of an unregistered type would have been dropped without a word

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / audit. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found writing the import test.**

**Observed.** The first version of the picture import wrote its audit record as
`design_asset_imported`, a type the event contract did not list. Design writes
audit events inside `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` so that a failing audit
never fails the owner's change, which meant the refused event left no trace.

**Fixed.** `design_asset_imported` is registered in `raiker/contracts/models.py`
and described in the [event catalog](../architecture/EVENT_CATALOG.md); the
import test asserts the indexed event exists.

**Evidence.** `test_the_owners_picture_is_an_import_asset_with_no_provider`
fails without the registration and passes with it.

## FIXED-1012 — Off-machine models needed an environment allowlist as well as the owner's connection

**Severity: High. Area: Models / authorization. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — owner request; [ADR-0004](../adr/ADR-0004-connection-bound-model-authorization.md).**

**Observed.** A provider the owner had connected on the Models page still needed
its host in `RAIKER_MODEL_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST` for provider-backed embeddings,
memory indexing, image generation and the hosted/private connectivity checks,
which refused with `model_egress_denied:no_allowlist` /
`egress_denied:no_allowlist`. Conversely, an environment key plus that variable
reached a provider the owner had never connected in the product.

**Root cause.** Two destination checks: the factory's connection-scoped host,
and a process-wide hostname glob list read independently in four places. The
list matched hostnames, not origins, so a port or scheme change still matched.

**Fixed.** `endpoint_policy.authorize_model_destination` and `canonical_origin`
replace `model_egress_allowlist` / `enforce_model_egress`. Every off-machine
model construction requires the owner's saved connection for that profile and
the canonical origin (scheme, host, effective port) it is bound to — the
connection's endpoint, or the profile's shipped endpoint for a key-only
connection. An `endpoint_env` override cannot move it. Explicit revocation of
the hosted/private gate still wins. The variable is ignored and named once in
the log (never its value). The `model_egress_allowlist_configured` read-model
field is gone; the Models posture shows connected off-machine providers. The
connect dialog offers **Use the key from `<VARIABLE>`** to turn an environment
key into a connection without the key reaching the page. Integrity-sweep
baselines that recorded a model allowlist are read without it.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_connection_authorization.py` (51, EGR-01 to
EGR-28), `tests/test_phase_4_hosted_model_runtime.py`,
`tests/test_phase_7_model_provider_runtime.py`, `tests/test_image_generation.py`,
`ModelsView.test.ts` (environment key), `ModelChip.test.ts`,
`providerErrors.test.ts`. Live: `web/e2e/model-connection-authorization-live.spec.ts`
2/2 on a fresh workspace with `RAIKER_MODEL_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST` set to an
unrelated host — one log notice, neither the variable's value nor the key in
the log or `/api/models`
(`docs/screenshots/2026-10-20-model-connection-authorization/`). Against a real
provider, `model-connection-anthropic-live.spec.ts` 4/4: an identity-linked
Anthropic key and workspace ID entered in **Connect** reached *can reach* and
answered a Haiku 4.5 turn with no allowlist anywhere
([live record](../architecture/WEB_APP_LIVE_TEST.md#result--2026-10-20-model-connection-authorization-hosted-anthropic-haiku-45)).

## FIXED-1013 — The connectivity checks took their destination and path from the action

**Severity: High. Area: Models / executors / security. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** `hosted_model_runtime` / `private_network_model_runtime`
`connectivity_check` read `endpoint` and `models_path` from action arguments and
issued a GET to their concatenation. The environment allowlist was the only
thing between a model-proposed URL and the request.

**Fixed.** The action names a `profile_id`. `endpoint`, `models_path`, `url`,
`base_url` and `path` are refused by name (`argument_not_accepted:<name>`). The
executor resolves the acting principal's own connection and gates through the
factory, checks the endpoint class, and lists models through the provider
adapter's route (no redirects, capped body, 15 s). Artifacts: profile id,
provider, endpoint kind, model count.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_phase_4_hosted_model_runtime.py` (destination
arguments ×5, cross-principal, unconnected, private HTTP, governed end to end).

## FIXED-1014 — Model image requests followed redirects with the API key

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / transport / security. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** `sandbox.post_json` and `post_multipart` checked the host and then
used `urllib.request.urlopen`, which follows a redirect and re-sends the
request headers, `Authorization` included, to the new host.

**Fixed.** Both send through `_open_without_redirects` (the `_NoRedirect`
handler now shared with MCP) and report `redirect_refused:<status>`. httpx
provider clients already followed no redirects; the pool now says so
explicitly and a test asserts it.

**Evidence.** `test_egr12_egr13_urllib_model_helper_refuses_a_redirect`,
`test_egr12_egr13_provider_http_client_does_not_follow_a_redirect` — loopback
servers, the redirect target receives nothing. The same defect in the connector
GET helper is open as [BUG-350](TO_BE_FIXED.md#bug-350--the-connector-get-helper-follows-redirects-with-the-owners-token).

## FIXED-1015 — Image generation could send a key saved for another endpoint to the provider's image host

**Severity: Medium. Area: Design / image runtime. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The image executor took the key from the saved connection or the
environment and posted it to the fixed OpenAI/Gemini image host, whatever
endpoint that connection was saved for, and an environment key with no
connection was enough. A revoked hosted gate did not stop it.

**Fixed.** A saved connection for the profile is required
(`model_connection_required`), the hosted gate must not be revoked
(`hosted_provider_requires_explicit_policy`), and the connection must be bound
to the provider's image origin (`image_connection_origin_mismatch`). Requests
are held to that one host and refuse redirects.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_image_generation.py`, `tests/test_image_lineage.py`,
contract case `/api/images`.

## FIXED-1016 — Revoking a model gate did not stop the next call of a running turn

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / lifecycle. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** `AgentGateway`, `owner_model_runtime` and the embedding executor
computed the provider policy once when their router was built, so a turn that
made several model calls kept using hosted models after the owner turned the
gate off.

**Fixed.** `ModelRouter(runtime_policy_resolver=…)` re-reads the gates for every
provider build; connections were already read per call. Pooled clients carry no
credential, so nothing cached can restore a revoked authorization. A request
already sent completes; nothing new starts.

**Evidence.** `test_a_gate_revoked_mid_turn_stops_the_next_call`,
`test_egr21_a_connection_deleted_mid_session_denies_the_next_request`,
`test_egr16_egr22_authorized_embedding_uses_the_current_saved_key`.

## FIXED-1017 — The advisor ignored the owner's saved connection

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / advisor. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The advisor's router had no connection resolver, so a hosted
advisor worked only with an environment key and the environment allowlist —
never with the key the owner saved on the Models page.

**Fixed.** The consult resolves the acting owner's connection for the advisor
profile, like every other model call.

**Evidence.** `test_egr28_the_advisor_uses_the_owners_connection_or_nothing`.

## FIXED-1018 — A custom endpoint could not be on the owner's network or the internet

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / custom endpoints. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found reviewing FIXED-935.**

**Observed.** FIXED-935 says a custom endpoint's address decides its gate, but
`validate_endpoint_policy` refused any non-loopback address on the
`generic-openai-compatible` profiles (`private_network_requires_network_and_egress_policy`,
`hosted_endpoint_requires_egress_policy`) because they do not declare
`requires_egress_policy`.

**Fixed.** `local_only` is the profile-level restriction on where an endpoint
may point; authorization is the connection and the gates. `requires_egress_policy`
stays declarative metadata (and OpenRouter's declaration check). Hosted HTTP
still needs `allow_remote_http`.

**Evidence.** `test_egr02_saved_private_network_connection_is_allowed`,
`test_a_custom_endpoint_may_be_an_owner_named_hosted_service`,
`test_a_local_only_profile_is_never_pointed_off_the_machine`,
`test_egr14_hosted_http_endpoint_is_refused_without_transport_permission`.

## FIXED-1019 — A loopback model request could be handed to an environment proxy

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Pooled provider clients used httpx's default `trust_env=True` for
every origin, so with `HTTP_PROXY` set and no `NO_PROXY`, a local Ollama or
llama.cpp request would go to the proxy. `local_service` already refused this
for liveness checks.

**Fixed.** Loopback origins get `trust_env=False`; hosted origins keep the
owner's proxy settings. Documented in the threat model and the hardening plan.

**Evidence.** `test_egr24_pooled_clients_follow_owner_proxies_except_for_loopback`.

## FIXED-1020 — Permissions said Hosted models was off above a provider that had just answered

**Severity: Medium. Area: Permissions / models. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live (LC-03).**

**Observed (live, 2026-10-20).** With Anthropic connected and a Haiku 4.5 turn
just answered, **Permissions → Hosted models** read *Off · Ask me* and *No —
Raiker cannot use this on this account*, and offered only **Turn on**. The
Models posture beside it read *On (by connection)*. The owner had no direct way
to make the explicit revocation that outranks every connection: the only
control on the row was the opposite one.

**Root cause.** A saved connection is the owner's consent to the hosted and
private-network gates (`provider_runtime_policy_from_gates`), but the gate view
asked only the capability admission read, which does not know about
connections. FIXED-322 had given the Models page the enforcing answer; the
Permissions row still showed the stored one.

**Fixed.** `CapabilityGateView` gains `enabled_by_connection`, asked of the same
policy read every model call makes, and `enforced_enabled` includes it for the
two model gates. The row shows **On by connection**, answers *Yes — on because
you connected a provider in Models*, explains that turning it off stops every
provider it covers while the connections stay saved, and offers **Turn off**.
After it, the posture reads *Off* and a connected card reads **Policy blocked**.

**Evidence.** `test_permissions_report_hosted_models_on_by_connection_and_revocable`,
`permissionLanguage.test.ts` (on by connection, revocable), live LC-03 in
`model-connection-anthropic-live.spec.ts`
(`docs/screenshots/2026-10-20-model-connection-anthropic/04a`, `04`, `05`).

## FIXED-1021 — A hosted model name was dialled wherever its DNS answer pointed (was BUG-349)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — closes
[BUG-349](TO_BE_FIXED.md) and the plan `MODEL_TRANSPORT_SECURITY_HARDENING.md`
(D1, NET-01, NET-02, NET-12), which is retired with this entry.**

**Observed.** ADR-0004 binds an off-machine model request to the origin of the
owner's saved connection, but the name was resolved by httpx at connect time
and never checked: a hosted name answering `10.0.0.5` or `127.0.0.1` was sent
the owner's key.

**Fixed.** `raiker/models/transport_guard.py` — `resolve_for_dial` resolves the
host once and classifies **every** answer against the connection's declared
class with `web_policy`'s classifier (`unwrap_address`, `address_is_reachable`,
`literal_address`; no second classifier). Hosted: every answer public, else
`model_dial_refused:non_public_address` (CGNAT `100.64/10` included). Home lab:
private, ULA or shared space; a public answer is
`public_address_for_private`, a loopback one `loopback_for_private`. Local:
loopback only. One refused answer refuses the dial. An unresolvable name stays
a connection failure.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_model_transport_guard.py` NET-01, NET-02 (loopback,
`::1`, mapped `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, CGNAT), NET-06, NET-07, NET-12; live MT-03
(`model-transport-guard-live.spec.ts`): a hosted name resolving to `10.0.0.5`
reads *Raiker refused to connect: this hosted provider's name resolved to a
private, loopback or link-local address* on the card.

## FIXED-1022 — A second DNS answer could move the dialled address (DNS rebinding)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D2, NET-03, acceptance 2 and 6).**

**Fixed.** `GuardedNetworkBackend` is the httpcore network backend of every
directly dialled pooled client (`ModelTransport`). It dials the address that
passed, in resolver order and only among passing answers; httpcore keeps the
URL's name for SNI, certificate verification and `Host`. Each new connection is
resolved once; a kept-alive connection was checked when opened, so a pooled
request pays for no lookup. httpx 0.28 has no backend hook, so the transport's
pool is replaced by an identical one with the guard, and a test pins that
against the locked httpx/httpcore.

**Evidence.** `test_net03_a_rebinding_answer_cannot_move_the_dialled_address`,
`test_answers_are_tried_in_order_and_only_among_those_that_passed`,
`test_the_pinned_dial_keeps_the_name_on_the_request` (a real loopback server:
two requests, one lookup, one connection, `Host` is the name),
`test_router_turn_refusal_happens_before_any_socket`,
`test_the_pool_replacement_is_pinned_to_the_locked_httpx`; live MT-01/MT-02 — a
real Anthropic catalogue, preflight and Haiku 4.5 turn through the pinned dial.

## FIXED-1023 — The image helpers resolved their hosted name twice

**Severity: Low. Area: Design / image runtime / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D2, urllib half).**

**Fixed.** `post_json` and `post_multipart` take `dial_kind`; the image
executor passes `remote_hosted`. A direct HTTPS request resolves once, checks
every answer and dials through `web_policy.pinned_https_opener(..., direct=True)`
(new: no proxy handler beside a pinned connection) with redirects still
refused. A proxied request goes to the proxy unpinned.

**Evidence.** `test_image_helper_refuses_a_hosted_name_that_resolves_privately`,
`test_image_helper_dials_the_address_that_passed`,
`test_image_helper_through_a_proxy_is_not_pinned`; `test_image_generation.py`
asserts the generation call asks for a hosted dial.

## FIXED-1024 — A cloud metadata service could be saved as a model destination

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D3, NET-04, NET-05).**

**Fixed.** `169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`,
`metadata.google.internal` and `metadata.azure.com` are refused for every class
with no opt-in: by name or literal when the connection is validated
(`refuse_metadata_destination` in the factory), and by resolved answer at dial
time.

**Evidence.** NET-04, NET-05, `test_a_saved_metadata_endpoint_is_refused_on_the_card`;
live MT-05 — saving `http://169.254.169.254/v1` with the link-local box ticked
is refused in the Connect dialog with `model_dial_refused:metadata_address`.

## FIXED-1025 — A link-local home-lab server had no owner opt-in

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / custom endpoints. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D3).**

**Fixed.** Link-local answers (`169.254/16`, `fe80::/10`) are refused by default
(`link_local_address`). The custom-endpoint dialog gains **Allow a link-local
address**, saved as `allow_link_local` on the connection
(`ModelConnectionRequest.allow_link_local`), shown back as
`ModelProfileView.allows_link_local` and prefilled on reconnect. Pooled clients
are keyed by the rule, so the opt-in never leaks to another connection.

**Evidence.** `test_link_local_needs_the_owners_per_connection_opt_in`,
`test_bug349_link_local_opt_in_is_saved_with_the_connection_and_shown`,
`test_the_pool_keys_clients_by_dial_rule`; live MT-04 (refused, then dialled
once ticked — the card then reports the server, not a policy refusal) and MT-06
(prefilled, dark theme, 390 px, no overflow).

## FIXED-1026 — The proxy route was httpx's implicit choice, and home-lab traffic could be proxied

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D4, NET-08, NET-09; supersedes FIXED-1019's mechanism).**

**Fixed.** `transport_guard.proxy_for` decides the route explicitly: a hosted
origin honours `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` minus `NO_PROXY`; a
loopback or private-network origin is always dialled directly. Pooled clients
use `trust_env=False` and an explicit `ModelTransport`, so httpx reads no proxy,
netrc or certificate setting of its own.

**Evidence.** NET-08 (loopback answers with both proxies set),
`test_a_private_network_origin_bypasses_the_proxy`, NET-09 (a real CONNECT
proxy is asked for `api.example.com:443`, never shown the key),
`test_egr24_pooled_clients_follow_owner_proxies_except_for_loopback`.

## FIXED-1027 — A keyed plain-HTTP model request could go through a proxy

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D4, NET-10).**

**Fixed.** `ModelTransport` refuses a request carrying a credential header over
`http://` through a proxy (`model_dial_refused:credential_over_http_proxy`);
the image helpers refuse the same. HTTPS through a proxy is a tunnel and stays.

**Evidence.** `test_net10_a_keyed_plain_http_request_through_a_proxy_is_refused`.

## FIXED-1028 — Nothing stopped a key being attached to another origin; TLS name checking was untested

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / transport. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D5, NET-11).**

**Fixed.** `ModelTransport` refuses a credentialed request whose origin is not
the one its client was opened for (`model_credential_origin_mismatch`), so an
adapter that ever builds an absolute URL elsewhere fails closed. A test proves a
certificate for another name fails the pinned handshake before any byte of the
request — or the key — reaches the server.

**Evidence.** `test_a_credential_is_only_attached_to_the_clients_own_origin`,
`test_net11_a_certificate_for_another_name_is_refused_before_headers_are_sent`.

## FIXED-1029 — The Models page did not say whether a request went through a proxy

**Severity: Low. Area: Models / UI. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (plan D4).**

**Fixed.** `ModelProfileView.proxy_route` is the proxy's `host:port` (never its
URL, which can carry a password) or `""`. Each off-machine card's posture line
ends *Direct connection* or *Through your proxy (host:port)*, and the
**Off-machine provider posture** gains **Through your proxy**.

**Evidence.** `test_the_models_page_names_the_proxy_without_its_password`; live
MT-01 — on this host Anthropic reads *Direct connection* (`NO_PROXY` covers it),
fourteen other hosted cards *Through your proxy (127.0.0.1:33773)*, and the
posture *Yes — 14 hosted profiles via 127.0.0.1:33773*.

## FIXED-1030 — A refused dial, and other classified denials, read as "enable its gate"

**Severity: Medium. Area: Models / UI / turns. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 (BUG-349's required user-interface outcome).**

**Observed.** A refusal raised as a policy error lists as `policy_denied`, and
Models **Test**, the model picker and first-run setup each said *enable its
gate first* for every one — including `model_connection_origin_mismatch` and the
new dial refusals, on a gate that was already on. A turn's connection failure
also still told the owner to check the retired *egress allowlist*.

**Fixed.** `ProviderDialRefusedError` (a `ProviderPolicyError`) carries
`model_dial_refused:<detail>`. `providerErrors.ts` explains each detail; all
three `policy_denied` branches prefer classified guidance and keep the gate
sentence only for an unexplained denial. `provider_failure_message` says, per
detail, that it is *a policy refusal, not a network fault*, and
`provider_connection_failed` now names the endpoint instead of the allowlist.

**Evidence.** `providerErrors.test.ts` (dial refusals),
`ModelsView.test.ts` (*explains a refused dial in the picker as an address, not
a gate*), `test_a_dial_refusal_keeps_its_own_code_and_sentence`; live MT-03,
MT-04 assert neither *enable its gate* nor *could not be reached* appears.

## FIXED-1031 — A durable preference reached a turn only when the prompt shared its words (MEM-BRIEF-01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / context. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Ambient recall was search only: an approved preference ("British spelling", "the standup is on Thursday") reached a turn only when the prompt happened to share its words, so the same owner fact was present on one turn and absent on the next.

**Fixed.** `raiker/memory/brief.py` builds the versioned `memory-brief-v1` projection of approved encrypted records — never a second store. Eligibility runs before ranking (approved, active, owner-held, search enabled, in scope, confidence ≥ 0.6, neither labelled nor *reading* secret- or credential-like); priority is pinned → written or corrected by the owner → confidence → trust → freshness → id; the budget is 8 items and 400 tokens, with one record cut at 280 characters. Every item names its `memory_id`, provenance, trust label, freshness and truncation reason, and a record the budget leaves out is reported with `max_items` or `token_budget`. The gatherer adds it as a `memory_brief` source ranked above searched recall, labelled untrusted data, and records its ids in the turn recall ledger so **Remembered** can correct or forget them.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_brief_and_recall_mode.py` (eligibility, provenance, deterministic order, budget reasons, labelled data that grants nothing); live RT-MEM-BRIEF.

## FIXED-1032 — Ambient recall could not be turned down, and no answer said which recall it ran under (MEM-MODE-02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / UI. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The only control over ambient recall was Incognito (all or nothing), and nothing in the transcript said whether a turn had searched memory, used a brief, or had memory switched off.

**Fixed.** `memory_settings.recall_mode` (`off`, `brief`, `search_when_relevant`; default `search_when_relevant`, the behaviour every install already had) with `PUT /api/memory/recall-mode` (human-only, unknown modes refused with 409) and **Memory → Recall & indexing → Recall mode**. The gatherer resolves the mode once; Incognito wins over all three. Each turn records `turn_memory_disclosures` — mode, what ran, Incognito, the retrieval backend and counts of what the budget let in — returned with `GET /api/sessions/{id}/recall`. The strip under an answer reads **Remembered *n* · Brief + search**, or one quiet line (*Memory: Brief only · nothing recalled*, *Memory not used: Incognito is on*), and opened says the backend and how many memories the brief left out.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_brief_and_recall_mode.py` (each mode, Incognito override, budget-true counts, route and owner-scoped disclosure), `memoryRecallMode.test.ts`, `RecallStrip.test.ts`, `MemoryView.test.ts`; live RT-MEM-BRIEF.

## FIXED-1033 — History search returned a pasted credential, an order that could change, and ran under Incognito (MEM-HISTORY-03)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / conversation recall. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** `conversation_search` returned an old exchange's text unredacted, so a token pasted months ago came back into a turn; exchanges recorded in the same instant could come back in a different order; and the tool answered while Incognito was on, although the guide says Incognito disables cross-conversation recall.

**Fixed.** `search_conversation_turns` breaks every tie by `turn_id`. Each result's window and match pass through the context redactor and carry `redacted`. Under Incognito the tool answers `withheld: incognito` instead of an empty list that would read as "never discussed". Results stay at most 25 of 1,200 characters, labelled `untrusted_conversation_data`, and nothing is written to memory.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_history_boundary.py` (tie order, masking, bounds, Incognito, owner isolation, no promotion).

## FIXED-1034 — `memory_search` returned as many memories as the model asked for, Incognito or not

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / tools. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Found while doing MEM-HISTORY-03.** The broker passed `int(max_results)` straight through, so one call could ask for the whole archive, and the tool ignored Incognito.

**Fixed.** The requested count is clamped to `MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS` (50), a non-number falls back to 20, and under Incognito the tool answers `withheld: incognito`. `memory_get` and the Memory page, which read one named record, are unchanged.

**Evidence.** `test_memory_search_clamps_the_requested_count`, `test_memory_search_is_withheld_under_incognito`.

## FIXED-1035 — There was no contract an external memory provider would have to meet (MEM-ADAPTER-04)

**Severity: Low. Area: Memory / security. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The decision allows a future external memory adapter only under opt-in egress, redaction, provenance mapping, scope propagation, local degradation, deletion reconciliation, pinned versions and audit — none of which existed as code or a threat model.

**Fixed.** `raiker/memory/adapter.py`: `MemoryAdapter` protocol, a disabled-by-default `MemoryAdapterPolicy`, `prepare_adapter_payload` (only approved, active, owner-held, allowed-scope, allowed-class records; secret- and credential-like never; redacted; six fields only), `query_with_local_fallback` (pinned version, returned ids limited to those sent, `degraded` local answer on any fault) and `reconcile_deletions` (only an explicit receipt confirms; the rest stay `pending`). Audits hold ids and counts, never text. [Memory adapter threat model](../threat-models/memory-adapter.md). **No provider is integrated or enabled.**

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_adapter_contract.py`.

## FIXED-1036 — The memory key had no runbook, and nothing checked the key stays out of memory (MEM-KEY-05)

**Severity: Low. Area: Memory / storage / docs. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Where the SQLCipher key comes from, how to verify and restore an encrypted backup, what machine loss means, and how to read the key-page posture were spread over code comments and a backups section.

**Fixed.** [The memory key and recovery](../guide/memory.md#the-memory-key-and-recovery) in the memory guide: key source and `store_key_missing`, keeping a copy of `app.key`, verify, restore, machine loss, the export/import route in place of rotation ([BUG-354](TO_BE_FIXED.md#bug-354--the-workspace-key-cannot-be-rotated-in-place)), and the `cipher_memory_security` posture fields.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_key_never_leaves.py` — the key and its derived form appear in no database bytes, memory export, log line or adapter payload.

## FIXED-1037 — Two contradictory memories that matched equally came back in id order (MEM-EVAL-06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Memory / retrieval / evaluation. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The recall evaluation needed a corpus that runs through the real context assembly. Its first run found that an inferred "standup is Monday" (confidence 0.7) ranked ahead of the owner's "standup is Thursday" (1.0) because hybrid recall broke a score tie by memory id.

**Fixed.** `raiker/memory/recall_evaluation.py` (`memory-recall-eval-v2`): nine synthetic cases — preference recall, stale-fact correction, contradictory memories, forgotten-memory non-resurrection, prompt-injection content, owner isolation, project isolation, Incognito and budget truncation — through `ContextGatherer`, scoring precision, provenance completeness and unsafe-recall rate. `retrieve_hybrid_memory` now breaks a tie by confidence, then recency, then id.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_memory_recall_evaluation_v2.py` — precision 1.0, provenance completeness 1.0, unsafe-recall rate 0.0.

## FIXED-1038 — The answer's recall backend read [REDACTED_SECRET]

**Severity: Low. Area: Memory / API / UI. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live in RT-MEM-03.**

**Observed.** Opened, the strip under an answer read *Recall mode: Search when relevant · searched [REDACTED_SECRET]*. The disclosure joined its labels as `memory-brief-v1+sqlite-fts5+raiker-local-hash-v1`, one unbroken 49-character token, and the response redactor masks a token that long as a possible secret — the same class as [FIXED-993](#fixed-993--a-build-handoffs-file-name-reached-the-page-as-redacted_secret) and [FIXED-1005](#fixed-1005--a-skipped-tokens-name-reached-the-page-as-redacted).

**Fixed.** The gatherer joins the labels with ` + `, so no part reaches the redactor's length; the page trims each part. The redactor is unchanged.

**Evidence.** `test_each_mode_assembles_exactly_what_it_says` asserts every part is under 40 characters; `memoryRecallMode.test.ts`; live RT-MEM-03 reads *searched sqlite-fts5 + raiker-local-hash-v1*.

## FIXED-1039 — An outcome could live only in a chat transcript; there was no durable goal (GOAL-01, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / storage. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The personal-agent specification's first delivery row, PA-D01, was *Planned*: nothing could hold an outcome across sessions. A task held one objective and a run; there was no record of success criteria, a plan of steps, or which tasks were working toward the same result.

**Fixed.** Migration `RAIKER-2121-goals-and-execution-profiles` adds owner-scoped `goals`, `goal_criteria`, `goal_steps` and `goal_events` (`raiker/goals/store.py`). A goal's steps link to ordinary tasks by `task_id`; every owner change names the revision it was made against and is compared-and-set, so a second tab acting on an older copy is refused with `goal_revision_stale`. `goal_events` keeps ids, states and counts only — never a step's instruction. Another owner's goal reads as never issued.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_goals_and_execution_profiles.py` (`test_an_edit_over_an_older_revision_is_refused`, `test_another_owners_goal_reads_as_never_issued`); contract cases in `tests/contract_cases/goals.py`.

## FIXED-1040 — Nothing said which goal states exist or what each may do (GOAL-02, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / lifecycle. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The specification names ten goal states and requires the server to own lifecycle and permitted transitions, with waiting reasons kept apart so an approval is never called a failure. No such vocabulary existed.

**Fixed.** `raiker/goals/lifecycle.py` publishes `draft`, `ready`, `running`, `waiting`, `paused`, `completed`, `partial`, `failed`, `stopped`, `archived`, the actions each allows (served as `allowed_actions` with every goal), the owner-facing reason for each wait or pause, and how a linked task's status maps to a step state. An unknown task status reads as waiting, never as finished; a missing task reads as failed.

**Evidence.** `test_every_state_publishes_its_actions_and_unknown_task_status_never_reads_done`; `goalPresentation.test.ts` (*draws only the buttons the server allows*).

## FIXED-1041 — An owner could not describe an outcome, its criteria and its steps (GOAL-03, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / API. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** There was no intake: no way to say what a good result is, how it will be known, and which steps lead there.

**Fixed.** `POST /api/goals` creates a **draft** (up to 12 criteria and 12 steps); `PUT /api/goals/{id}/plan` edits a draft over the revision the owner saw. A step may run only after steps listed before it, so a plan can never contain a cycle; a Build step needs the goal filed in a project, the same rule Build tasks have. A draft has no permission to run — Start is not among its actions. All goal mutations are human-only and there is no model tool for any of them.

**Evidence.** `test_intake_is_a_draft_with_no_permission_to_run`, `test_a_plan_cannot_depend_forward_or_reach_build_without_a_project`, `test_profile_and_goal_changes_are_human_only`; live RT-GOAL-02.

## FIXED-1042 — Accepting a plan named no boundary for the work (GOAL-04, PA-D01, PA-D02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / execution profiles. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The specification requires an owner-accepted plan before anything runs, under the execution profile Settings binds. Nothing could be accepted, and nothing pinned which boundary a goal would run under.

**Fixed.** `POST /api/goals/{id}/accept` moves a draft to **ready** only with at least one required criterion and one step, refuses a *met when its steps finish* criterion no step counts toward (it could never be met), and refuses with `no_execution_profile` until Settings has a profile. It pins the profile's id and version and copies its budget onto the goal.

**Evidence.** `test_accept_needs_a_profile_from_settings_and_pins_its_version`, `test_a_steps_finish_criterion_with_no_step_cannot_be_accepted`; live RT-GOAL-02, RT-GOAL-03.

## FIXED-1043 — A goal could not start work, and nothing would carry it from one step to the next (GOAL-05, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / coordinator / scheduler. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The target is a coordinator around existing task execution — never a second tool broker — that selects a due step, reserves budget and starts an ordinary governed turn.

**Fixed.** `raiker/goals/coordinator.py`. **Start** is the owner's intent to run; the coordinator files each step whose dependencies have finished as an ordinary queued task through the same `create_task` path a task filed by hand takes, so every tool call still goes through the policy engine, broker, approvals and runtime authority. The scheduler advances running goals on each tick before it claims due work, and again after a batch settles, so the next step is filed as soon as the one before it finishes.

**Evidence.** `test_start_files_only_due_steps_as_ordinary_tasks`, `test_completion_needs_every_mandatory_criterion_not_just_finished_steps` (the second step is filed only after the first finished); live RT-GOAL-04.

## FIXED-1044 — A goal could not say what it was waiting on (GOAL-06, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / read model. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** A step parked on an approval must make its goal *wait* with that reason, not fail, and a parent may not read as complete while a step is open.

**Fixed.** Each pass reads every linked task back: a step waiting for a decision, an answer, delegated work or a pause makes the goal **waiting** with that named reason; one running makes it **running**; a step whose dependency failed or stopped becomes *will not start* rather than running against a missing result. The goal settles only when every step has.

**Evidence.** `test_a_step_parked_on_a_decision_makes_the_goal_wait_with_that_reason`, `test_a_failed_step_blocks_its_dependants_and_nothing_met_reads_failed`; `GoalsView.test.ts`.

## FIXED-1045 — Nothing could tell a finished outcome from finished steps (GOAL-07, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / outcome assessment. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Completed must mean every mandatory criterion has evidence; partial must name what is unmet; and no model statement may complete a goal.

**Fixed.** Each criterion names how it is met: **Met when its steps finish** (deterministic: every step counting toward it finished, recorded as *Its steps finished* with the tasks' ids — a record that they finished, not a judgement that the result is good) or **You confirm it** (`POST /api/goals/{id}/criteria/{criterion_id}/confirm`, recorded as *Confirmed by you* with the owner's note). A goal whose steps settled reads **completed** only when every required criterion has evidence, **partial** when some do, **failed** when none do; confirming on a partial goal reassesses it.

**Evidence.** `test_completion_needs_every_mandatory_criterion_not_just_finished_steps`; live RT-GOAL-04, RT-GOAL-05.

## FIXED-1046 — There was no single Stop for an outcome's work (GOAL-08, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / interrupts. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Stop must reach every active step and what it delegated, prevent new claims, and report what had finished.

**Fixed.** `POST /api/goals/{id}/stop` stops each linked task through `InterruptController` with its delegation cascade, marks unsettled steps stopped, and answers with steps finished, steps stopped and tasks stopped. The scheduler re-checks a goal step just before running it: a step whose goal is no longer running is cancelled and never starts.

**Evidence.** `test_stop_reaches_every_linked_task_and_nothing_new_is_filed`, `test_the_scheduler_does_not_run_a_step_of_a_stopped_goal`; live RT-GOAL-06.

## FIXED-1047 — Pausing and continuing an outcome had no defined meaning (GOAL-09, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / interrupts. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Pause must start nothing new; continuing must recheck scope before any further work.

**Fixed.** **Pause** files nothing new and parks step tasks not yet claimed; a run already in flight finishes its current turn (Stop is the control that abandons one), and the page says so. **Resume** rechecks the owner, the execution profile Settings binds now, every model the turn could fall back to, and the budget; only then are parked steps made due again, atomically on their status. A profile that changed is adopted on Resume or Start only after it admits the work, recorded as `goal_profile_repinned`.

**Evidence.** `test_pause_parks_unclaimed_steps_and_resume_rechecks_the_chain`, `test_start_after_settings_switched_the_profile_adopts_the_new_one`.

## FIXED-1048 — A goal had no budget across its steps (GOAL-10, PA-D01)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / budgets. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Goal budgets must be reserved before dispatch and reconciled after, across every child.

**Fixed.** A goal carries the profile's step-run limit and optional cost limit. A step run is reserved compared-and-set before its task is filed; when the limit is reached the goal pauses with *The goal's budget is used up*. Spend is reconciled from the usage ledger for the goal's own step conversations and priced the way the Models page prices it; a step's task carries the goal's remaining cost as its own per-run limit, so a run stops at its next safe boundary rather than only the next dispatch. Unpriced models are named.

**Evidence.** `test_the_step_run_budget_pauses_the_goal_before_the_next_dispatch`, `test_a_cost_budget_caps_each_step_run`; live RT-GOAL-04 (the detail's budget line).

## FIXED-1049 — There was nowhere to say where a goal's work may run (PROF-01, PA-D02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Execution profiles / Settings. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** PA-D02 was *Planned*. The specification makes Settings the only place an execution profile is created, changed, activated or bound, with templates **Private local**, **Balanced** and **Cloud-first** that remain inspectable profiles rather than hidden fallbacks.

**Fixed.** `raiker/goals/profiles.py` and `/api/execution-profiles`: versioned owner-scoped profiles of model placement (this machine, hosted, or both), an optional provider list, whether personal memory may go to a hosted model, and per-goal step-run and cost limits. A change writes the next version over the version the owner saw; the first profile becomes active; each change is audited. Every field is enforced — a profile admitting no model, or memory to a hosted model it refuses, is refused or corrected where it is set. **Settings → Execution profiles** offers the templates, edits a profile, makes one active and binds one to a project.

**Evidence.** `test_provider_allowlist_and_validation`; `ExecutionProfiles.test.ts`; live RT-GOAL-03, RT-GOAL-07.

## FIXED-1050 — Nothing stopped an outcome reaching a model the owner had ruled out (PROF-02, PA-D02)

**Severity: High. Area: Execution profiles / dispatch / memory. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** A local-only goal must stay local; a failed local model or unavailable host is a named blocker, not a reason to fall back; and a profile must decide which data classes travel with cloud work.

**Fixed.** Before a step is filed — and again in the scheduler just before it runs — every model the turn could actually run on, the owner's selected model **and every fallback in their sequence**, is judged by the goal's profile. A refusal names the provider and placement (*anthropic (hosted)*), files nothing, and leaves the goal waiting with a route to Settings; a refusal at run time cancels the unstarted task and refunds the run. Under a profile that keeps memory off hosted models, a step whose chain includes one has its conversation marked: the context gatherer recalls nothing (as under Incognito) and `memory_search`, `memory_list`, `memory_get`, `conversation_search` and `knowledge_graph` answer *withheld*. The goal reads back from the usage ledger which providers actually answered.

**Evidence.** `test_private_local_refuses_a_hosted_model_by_name_and_files_nothing`, `test_a_fallback_outside_the_profile_blocks_as_surely_as_the_primary`, `test_model_chain_judges_the_selected_model_and_every_fallback`, `test_the_scheduler_refuses_a_step_whose_chain_left_the_profile`, `test_balanced_withholds_memory_from_a_hosted_step_and_cloud_first_does_not`; live RT-GOAL-03, RT-GOAL-04.

## FIXED-1051 — Changing the boundary would have applied silently to work in flight (PROF-03, PA-D02)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Execution profiles / goals. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** A change to an active or project-bound profile must pause running goals at a safe boundary and revalidate before further work; a project may carry its own profile.

**Fixed.** Saving a profile version, changing the active profile or a project binding pauses every running or waiting goal whose pinned version is no longer the one Settings states, and the answer says how many it paused. The coordinator's own pass does the same if it finds the pinned and bound versions disagree. A goal filed in a project bound to a profile is accepted under that one.

**Evidence.** `test_a_profile_change_pauses_running_goals_at_a_safe_boundary`, `test_a_project_binding_wins_over_the_active_profile`; live RT-GOAL-07.

## FIXED-1052 — Goals had no page (UX-GOALS-01, PA-D06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / UI. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** The UX specification requires one view per goal with criteria, plan, task tree, blockers, budgets and Pause/Resume/Stop, controls only where the backend path exists, and the active profile as read-only context with a route to Settings.

**Fixed.** **Work → Goals** (`GoalsView.svelte`, `goalPresentation.ts`): an intake form for outcome, criteria (how each is met, required or not) and steps (Chat or Build, runs after, counts toward); a list with state and reason; and a detail drawing the goal's own `allowed_actions`, each criterion's evidence with **Confirm met**, each step's state with **Open its task**, the pinned profile read-only (*Settings has changed it since…* when it has), the budget line, the providers that answered and the history. Progress is a count of finished steps, never a percentage. Stop asks once more. The layout reflows to one column at phone width.

**Evidence.** `GoalsView.test.ts`, `goalPresentation.test.ts`, `nav.test.ts`; live RT-GOAL-02 to RT-GOAL-06.

## FIXED-1053 — Home could not say which outcomes needed the owner (UX-GOALS-02, PA-D06)

**Severity: Medium. Area: Home / goals. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20.**

**Observed.** Home should answer what is progressing, what needs my decision and what finished.

**Fixed.** Home's **Goals** board groups goals into **Needs you** (ready to start, paused, partly done, or waiting on a decision, an answer or Settings), **In progress** and **Finished recently**, each linking to the goal's own page. Like readiness, a failed read keeps the last answer rather than erasing the board; drafts stay on Work → Goals.

**Evidence.** `WorkbenchView.test.ts` (*lists a goal that needs the owner*); live RT-GOAL-05.

## FIXED-1054 — A goal's steps ran on whatever an empty model selection resolved to

**Severity: High. Area: Goals / models / execution profiles. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live in RT-GOAL-03.**

**Observed.** On a fresh host with Anthropic connected and chosen for a Chat turn, **Start** under *Private local* was not refused. The step's task carried no model, so the turn would run on the owner's stored selection — on a fresh workspace the packaged default, `ollama-local-openai-compatible` with its `<model>` placeholder — and the profile check judged that placeholder, not the model the owner meant. The step then failed against a model that was never set up, and the goal read **Failed**.

**Root cause.** A Chat turn names its model per turn; it does not change the stored selection a task without a model falls back to. The goal had nowhere to say which model its steps use.

**Fixed.** A goal names `model_profile` and `model`, chosen with the same model picker Tasks uses (the picker's shown model is taken when the owner does not open it, never a `<model>` placeholder). **Accept** refuses `goal_needs_model` or `goal_model_not_configured`; each step's task is filed on that model; the profile check judges that model followed by the owner's fallbacks. The goal's page says *Steps run on …*.

**Evidence.** `test_accept_needs_a_configured_model_and_steps_run_on_it`, `test_model_chain_starts_from_the_goals_own_model`; live RT-GOAL-03 refuses *anthropic (hosted)* and RT-GOAL-04 runs the step on Haiku 4.5.

## FIXED-1055 — A criterion's text box and a step's *counts toward* box had the same name

**Severity: Low. Area: Goals / accessibility. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found live in RT-GOAL-02.**

**Observed.** A screen reader and the live spec both found two controls called *Criterion 1*: the criterion's text field and the checkbox under step 1 that says it counts toward criterion 1.

**Fixed.** The fields are *Criterion 1 text* and *Criterion 1 is required*; the step checkboxes are *Step 2 runs after step 1* and *Step 1 counts toward criterion 1*, with the short visible label unchanged.

**Evidence.** Live RT-GOAL-02 fills each by its own name.

## FIXED-1056 — Goal and profile audit events would have been dropped without a word

**Severity: Medium. Area: Goals / audit. Status: Fixed 2026-10-20 — found writing the event catalogue entry.**

**Observed.** `AgentEvent` refuses an event type missing from `EVENT_TYPES`, and the coordinator's audit write is suppressed on failure so a logging fault cannot stop a goal. Together they meant every `goal_*` and `execution_profile_*` audit event raised and vanished: the goal's own history table recorded each change, the owner's audit log recorded none.

**Fixed.** The seventeen goal and profile event types are declared in `EVENT_TYPES`, including the three the coordinator builds from the outcome name.

**Evidence.** `test_every_goal_and_profile_change_reaches_the_audit_log` reads them back from the event index; `test_no_runtime_event_type_is_undeclared`.
